## Problem

Multiple developers see `PrivilegeGuard.sln.DotSettings` show up as a pending change in their working tree even though they never edit it. The newer ReSharper bundled with Visual Studio 2026 (the `ReSharperPlatformVs18` install) auto-applies a one-time settings migration on first solution open: it adds entries under a new `/Default/CodeStyle/Naming/CppNamingOptions/Rules/...` schema and stamps the migrator flag `IsMigratorApplied=True`. Because the migrated form has never been committed, every dev on VS 2026 keeps re-dirtying the same file.

## Solution

Commit the migrated DotSettings so ReSharper sees the migrator flag is already set and stops modifying the file on solution open. The migration is **additive** - the original `CppNaming/Rules` entries are preserved alongside the new `CppNamingOptions/Rules` entries - so devs still on older ReSharper / VS 2022 are unaffected.

Diff is +15 lines, 0 removals: 14 new rule entries under the new schema plus the `IsMigratorApplied` flag.

## Problem

EPM-52259 was a use-after-free that existed across ~15 call sites in the rules engine because the lifetime ownership convention (raw pointers handed back into smart-pointer-managed configs) was implicit and not enforced. The fix in PR #3690 closed the bug by moving lifetime ownership into the engine itself, but no AI assistant guidance currently exists to flag this bug class on future generation or review — making a regression in another subsystem easy.

## Solution

Add four review bullets to the two AI assistant configuration files in this repo, tight to the four points called out by the EPM-54379 RCA outcome:

- Methods returning raw pointers into reference-counted or smart-pointer-managed objects.
- Smart pointer going out of scope while a raw pointer derived from it is still in use.
- Concurrent access where one thread can free an object another thread references.
- Designs where each call site owns the lifetime of a shared object — prefer callee or shared-scope ownership.

Files touched:
- ``.claude/rules/global-cpp.md`` — new ``## Object Lifetime`` subsection, placed after Concurrency & Performance.
- ``.github/copilot-instructions.md`` — four bullets added to ``PR Review Points (Security & Risk)``, grouped after the existing concurrency bullet.

Wording is kept tight and bullet-only to match the existing terse style of both files. C++ only — the bug class is raw pointers into smart-pointer-managed objects, which doesn't translate cleanly to C#.

body: ## Problem The `add-jira-link` job in `🤖 PR Validation & Actions` runs `Build/scripts/AddJiraLinkToPRDescription.ps1`. Before posting the updated PR body it does: ```powershell $body = $body -replace '"', '\"' ``` PowerShell's native argument passing already quotes arguments correctly when invoking native commands, so this manual escape is unnecessary — and the resulting backslashes end up stored verbatim in the PR description. Every `"` the author wrote becomes `\"` after the workflow runs. You can see this on PR #3822, where strings like `"."`, `"localhost"`, `"this machine"` came out as `\".\"`, `\"localhost\"`, `\"this machine\"`. This applies to every PR description that has had the workflow run. The same escape also broke any image embeds in the description: GitHub's user-attachment URLs use `"`-quoted attributes inside `` tags, so the workflow rewrote them and broke the image rendering. ## Solution Drop the `-replace` line and write the body to a temp file, then pass it via `gh pr edit --body-file`. This is immune to argument quoting regardless of body contents — `"`, backticks, `$`, and so on all pass through verbatim. To prove the fix works end-to-end, this PR description deliberately includes literal double quotes — `"like this"`, `"and these"`, and a sentence containing `"."` (which is the spelling that broke #3822). After the workflow runs, all of these should remain unmodified rather than being rewritten as `\"...\"`. Embedded images are also confirmed working — verified separately on a test PR description with an `` embed that previously had its `src="..."` mangled. ### Out of scope Existing PRs whose bodies are already corrupted are not back-corrected by this change. A one-off cleanup pass could be done separately if there's appetite. ## Checklist > [!IMPORTANT] > __All PRs should follow our [Core Guidelines](https://beyondtrust.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PMFW/pages/780271678/EPM+Windows+Development+Strategy#Core-Guidelines). <!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Comparing two `std::wstring`/`std::wstring_view` values case-insensitively has no obvious entry point in the codebase today. The closest helper, `xstd::CaseInsensitiveStringEqualTo<std::wstring>`, lives in `xstd/CaseInsensitiveUnorderedSet.h` — a header named for set construction, which isn't where anyone reaching for \"compare two strings\" looks. Call sites either reach for `_wcsicmp`, build a one-off `towlower` lambda, or instantiate the functor directly. Needed for a follow-up change on EPM-48229.

## Solution

Add `xstd::Equals` overloads for `std::string_view` and `std::wstring_view` to `xstd/StringManip.h`, alongside the existing case-insensitive `BeginsWith` / `EndsWith`. `std::wstring`, `std::wstring_view`, and wide string literals all implicitly convert, so callers can pass any of them in either argument position.

- Wide path uses `std::towlower` (the right function for `wchar_t`; the latent narrow-`tolower`-on-`wchar_t` bug in `BeginsWith` / `EndsWith` is tracked separately under EPM-54170 and intentionally not touched here).
- Narrow path widens through `unsigned char` before `std::tolower` to avoid the UB / debug-CRT assert that occurs on bytes ≥ 0x80 when `char` is signed.

The existing `CaseInsensitiveStringHash` / `CaseInsensitiveStringEqualTo` functors in `CaseInsensitiveUnorderedSet.h` are left in place — they're still the right thing for `unordered_set` / `unordered_map` template arguments and the duplication is small.

15 new MSTest tests cover wide + narrow same/different case, length mismatch, empty inputs, owned/view/literal interop, plus a non-ASCII regression check (`Ł` vs `A`/`a`) and a high-byte safety check. Full `xstdTests` suite (99 tests) passes locally.

body:
## Problem

Three scenarios in `PMfW Regression - Filters` (the BIAzureADFilters feature) flake intermittently on slower endpoints (consistently ARM64):

- `BIPolicyIsAppliedBecauseUserMatchesAnAzureADGroupAndAWindowsGroup` — 50% (10/20)
- `BIPolicyIsAppliedBecauseUserMatchesAllAzureADGroups` — 40% (8/20)
- `BIPolicyIsAppliedBecauseUserMatchesAnAzureADGroup` — 40% (8/20)

The visible exception is a token-mismatch assertion fail:

```
Assert.IsTrue failed. FAIL: Token mismatch for process 'DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe'.
Checking for presence of 'BUILTIN\Administrators', expected match 'True', actual False
```

Root cause: the Background step `Given Privilege Management for Windows already knows about my user` (binding: `IdpGroupsBindings.PrivilegeManagementForWindowsAlreadyKnowsAboutMyUser`) launches a warmup `DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe` to trigger PMfW's first-time AzureAD group fetch from the mock BeyondInsight service, then waits with a fixed `Thread.Sleep(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(3))`. On ARM64 the fetch overruns the 3s budget, the cache directory for the test user's SID isn't populated, and when the test's subsequent `When I run 'DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe' ...` step launches the dummy app, PMfW evaluates the AzureAD group filter against an empty cache, the rule doesn't match, no admin token is added, and the assertion fails after its 20s `accesschk` retry loop.

The original author's comment on the binding explicitly notes this race (\"PMfW does not wait for the request to PMC to go through\") but used a fixed sleep instead of polling the completion signal.

## Solution

Snapshot `IdPGroupsCache.GetLastModifiedTime()` before launching the warmup process, then poll (Polly, 30 retries x 1s) until the mtime advances after the kill — proving the service has flushed the AzureAD fetch result to `%ProgramData%\Avecto\Privilege Guard\AzureADCache\<sid>\`.

Mirrors the existing `GroupsRefreshed` binding in the same file (lines 104-120). Reuses imports already present (`Polly`, `IdPGroupsCache`).

Alternative considered: bump the `Thread.Sleep` to 10-15s. Rejected — still non-deterministic, slow on the happy path, and would only mask the race for moderate latencies.

## Problem

`Upgrading_AdvancedParentTracking_GrandChildMatches` (and any test that calls `DeferredActions.ClickAppButton` / `AssertDummyOpenVisible`) was throwing `NullReferenceException(\"Windows list was empty, or contained only nulls\")` on Windows 11 ARM64 endpoints. All 8 observed failures across 4 nightly runs (2026-04-28 → 2026-05-05) hit five distinct ARM64 24H2/25H2 machines (`11-24H2AF26-A01/A05`, `11-25H2AF26-A01/A03/A04`); no x64 endpoint has reproduced.

Root cause: `DeferredActions.ClickAppButton` / `AssertDummyOpenVisible` call `Retry.WhileEmpty(() => app.GetAllTopLevelWindows(new UIA3Automation()))` to discover the DeferredDummyApp top-level window. The call inherits the framework-wide FlaUI default of 5s (`Retry.DefaultTimeout` in `CommonSetup.cs`). `DeferredDummyApp.exe` is a .NET Framework 4.8 x64 WinForms application; on Windows 11 ARM64 it runs under x64 emulation, which makes process startup and first-paint substantially slower than the 5s budget. When the timeout fires, `WhileEmpty` returns an empty array and the explicit `windows == null || windows.All(i => i == null)` guard throws.

## Solution

Pass an explicit 30-second `timeout:` argument to the two `Retry.WhileEmpty` calls in `DeferredActions.cs`. Local override only — the global FlaUI 5s default is unchanged, so other waits (which already pass on ARM64) are unaffected. 30s comfortably exceeds the observed ~12s emulation startup envelope while keeping bounded failure semantics if the window genuinely never appears. Consistent with similar overrides already in the framework (e.g. `NotificationPopup.cs:489` uses 60s for a `WhileNull` UI wait).

Alternative considered: bumping the global `Retry.DefaultTimeout` to 30s. Rejected — it would slow every framework retry across the suite, including paths that legitimately fail-fast.

## Problem

The `test-plan` skill's `SKILL.md` had grown to 506 lines, packing workflow logic, an ADF node reference, the full page template, test quality rules, and update-mode handling all into one always-loaded document. Users hit two recurring failure modes:

1. **Test content quality issues** — generated tests violated scope/format rules that were documented but buried at the bottom of the file.
2. **Field state misclassified** — step 4's \"is `customfield_10097` empty / has-test-plan / has-other-content\" decision went wrong, partly because the issue was fetched in markdown but the classification really needs ADF.

Sibling skills (`xray-create`, `fetch-epm-installer`, `crash-dump`) already follow a \"Claude does judgement, PowerShell does mechanics\" pattern. `test-plan` was the outlier.

## Solution

Three coordinated changes that simplify the skill without losing functionality:

1. **Split bulk reference material out of `SKILL.md`** (no content loss):
   - `references/adf-nodes.md` — relocated ADF node reference; loaded only when constructing ADF directly outside the script.
   - `references/page-template.md` — relocated page template + structured input schema for `Build-TestPlanPage.ps1`; loaded when generating a new plan.
   - `references/test-quality.md` — relocated quality rules; loaded **before** generating any tests, which addresses the \"rules buried at the bottom\" issue.

   `SKILL.md` is now ~200 lines and points at each reference at the exact step it's needed.

2. **Push deterministic mechanics into PowerShell scripts:**
   - `scripts/Get-TestPlanState.ps1` — classifies `customfield_10097` ADF deterministically. Eliminates the markdown-vs-ADF mismatch behind the misclassification bug.
   - `scripts/Build-TestPlanPage.ps1` — takes structured plan input and emits the full ADF page document with all boilerplate baked in (TOC, banner, Problem/Solution placeholders, Questions placeholder, STRIDE table skeleton, Accessibility checklist with the five fixed checks). Allocates unique `localId` values automatically. Validates input and rejects `PMfW`-prefixed test names, tests missing Given/When/Then, invalid `issueMaturity`, etc. — defense-in-depth against the test-quality issue alongside the prompt-side reference.
   - `scripts/Update-EvidenceField.ps1` — writes the link to `customfield_10097` for both empty and preserve-existing-content cases, working in ADF throughout.

3. **Targeted simplifications inside the workflow** (only behaviour changes; everything else is pure relocation):
   - **Always fetch `customfield_10097` in ADF** up-front. Removes the prior \"fetch in markdown then re-fetch in ADF\" footgun.
   - **Drop the \"Refinement update suggested\" panel feature** from update mode — was never asked for and a major source of complexity.
   - **Status banner**, **`[Added from Jira/PR/refinement]` prefixes**, and **backfill behaviour** all preserved.

4. **Working files now go to an OS temp dir** via `mktemp -d`, never inside the repo. SKILL.md spells out the `mktemp -d` + `cygpath -wa` + `rm -rf` pattern so future runs don't dump JSON artifacts into the working tree.

## Problem

`SystemSettings_Auth_MSI_ModifyUninstall_Variant0` (PMfW Regression - AppMatchingUninstallers) has been flaky at ~20% on `B-11-24H2-UAC-1` (Windows 11 24H2). Failed to get valid system settings window` at `Win10SystemSettings.LaunchAppsAndFeatures()`. Failure screenshots show the Settings app is open and on the Installed apps page — the matcher just doesn't see it within the 10s wait window.

The Settings app on Win11 22H2+ is WinUI 3 internally but is still hosted inside `ApplicationFrameWindow`, so the existing class-name match is valid (and passes ~80% of the time on 24H2). The failure mode is a slow-render race: on 24H2 the WinUI 3 host occasionally takes longer than 10s to register a top-level window the desktop UIA tree can see, so the matcher times out before the window is queryable.

## Solution

Bump the matcher timeout in `Win10SystemSettings.LaunchAppsAndFeatures` from 10s to 15s. This gives the WinUI 3 host enough headroom on 24H2 to register the top-level window before the matcher gives up.

This PR is a slimmer alternative to #3732 (same flake, same ticket): it keeps only the change that addresses the observed race and drops the speculative process-PID fallback, since today's class-name match is still valid on 24H2 and the fallback would have zero coverage until a future Windows build retired `ApplicationFrameWindow`.

`BeyondInsightIntegration`, `IdentityCore`, and `IdentityIntegration` have a `[BeforeTestRun]` hook calling `CommonSetup.TestRunSetup()` but no matching `[AfterTestRun]` hook, so `CommonTeardown.TestRunTeardown()` never runs.

`TestRunTeardown` does several things — `DeleteConfig`, `DisableLogging`, and `Directory.Delete` cleanup of fixture dirs (`BatchFiles`, `Configs`, `Content`, `Installers`, `Resources`, `TestResultFiles`, `AutoTempDir`). The first two are masked by per-scenario CRAFT snapshot revert, but the fixture-dir cleanup is observable today: `Configs`, `Content`, and `Resources` (~380 KB / ~15 files per machine) leak into per-machine `Artefacts/` uploads on `\fs01.btrusteng.com\ExecutionProduction\PMfW Regression - <suite>\<run-uuid>\Endpoints\<machine>\0_<suite>\Artefacts\` for these three suites — visibly absent for working suites like `AgentProtection`. Sanity-check: a sweep of all 49 suite projects confirms only these three are missing `[AfterTestRun]` (with `[BeforeTestRun]` present). Every other regression/smoke suite has the matching pair.

(Discovered while prototyping a code-coverage PoC that hooks into `TestRunSetup`/`TestRunTeardown` — the missing teardown half made the gap impossible to ignore — but the leak itself is pre-existing and ships in main today.)

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

The `find-build` composite action used by Run Test Suite and Auto Regression searched the 20 most recent `build.yml` runs filtered by the current branch. That made it impossible to dispatch a test workflow against a build produced on a different branch — for example, running tests on a feature branch against an installer that came from `main` — even though the AzDO pipeline this replaced supported version-by-anywhere lookups.

Concrete failure case: dispatching Run Test Suite from `nw/epm-52141/automation` with `build-identifier=26.2.1.10326` (a build produced on `rp/feat/epm-52139/retrieve_groups`) exited with `No Full Build with product version 26.2.1.10326 found on branch '<branch>'. Searched the 20 most recent runs.` See [run 25059981863](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25059981863).

## Solution

Resolve the build identifier via JFrog Artifactory metadata instead of walking GitHub Actions runs:

- **Product version** → property search on `product.version`, with a path-based fallback (`*/<version>/PMfW_*.zip`) for pre-#3764 builds whose Full Build ran before that property was set.
- **GitHub run ID** → property search on `github.run_id`.
- **`latest`** → property search on `github.branch`, sort by JFrog's built-in `created` timestamp descending, take newest. Per-repo `--limit=1 --sort-by=created --sort-order=desc` keeps the search Artifactory-side.

Search order across repos is `eng-generic-qa-local → eng-generic-dev-local`. For version/run-id, stop at the first repo with a hit; for `latest`, merge hits across both repos and pick the newest by `created`. `eng-generic-prod-local` is intentionally excluded — `certify-build` copies bundles there with `jf rt copy --flat`, which strips properties, into a layout (`epm-pmfw/<short>/<version>/`) that omits the `/client/` segment, so neither `--props` nor the action's path pattern match anything. The qa-local original of every certified build is still retained, so resolution falls through to the same artifact via qa-local.

Once resolved, the run still has to provide `_ServiceSymbols`, `_Automation`, `_AutomationNative`, and `_AutoInfrastructure` from the GitHub artifacts API (installers come from JFrog). Hard-fail with a clear error if any of those are missing — typically meaning retention has expired (default 90 days) or the publish step never completed.

Branch is now irrelevant to resolution. Both callers (`run-test-suite.yml`, `auto-regression.yml`) gain a single new input — `jfrog-token: ${{ secrets.JFROG_READONLY_PLAIN_ACCESS_TOKEN }}` — and the action's `run-id` / `product-version` outputs are unchanged, so downstream steps are untouched.

### Validation

**End-to-end against real workflow runs** — kicked off 3 Run Test Suite dispatches from this branch and inspected the `Find build` step output, then cancelled each one:

| # | Input | Result | Run |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `build-identifier=25133121456` (run-id) | `Resolved: run 25133121456, product version 26.2.1.267` from `eng-generic-qa-local/epm-pmfw/client/26.2/26.2.1.267/PMfW_26.2.zip` | [25161325241](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25161325241) |
| 2 | `build-identifier=26.2.1.267` (version) | `Resolved: run 25133121456, product version 26.2.1.267` from same path; stopped at qa-local on first hit | [25161323962](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25161323962) |
| 3 | `build-identifier=latest` on this PR branch (no Full Build exists) | Hard fail with `::error::No builds found in JFrog for branch 'fix/jfrog-driven-find-build-EPM-54334'. Run a Full Build on this branch first, or set use-latest-main=true to fall back to main.` | [25161322629](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/25161322629) |

**Local exhaustive scenarios against real JFrog** (resolve logic mirrored to a local script that calls the same `jf rt search` commands):

| # | Input | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | version `26.2.1.267` | resolves to run 25133121456 in qa-local on first hit |
| 2 | version `26.2.1.10407` | qa-local skipped, resolves in dev-local to run 25116337014 |
| 3 | run-id `25133121456` | resolves to version 26.2.1.267 in qa-local |
| 4 | run-id `25116337014` | qa-local skipped, resolves in dev-local |
| 5 | `latest` on `main` | resolves to qa-local newest (26.2.1.267) |
| 6 | `latest` on this PR branch | fails cleanly (no builds) |
| 7 | `latest` on dev branch `rp/feat/epm-52141/filter_matching` | resolves correctly from dev-local |
| 8 | bogus version `99.99.99.99` | fails cleanly through both prop and path search |
| 9 | bogus run-id `99999999999` | fails cleanly |
| 10 | garbage input `asdfqwer` | rejected with `Invalid build-identifier` |
| 11 | version `26.1.23.0` (present only in prod-local) | correctly unreachable — confirms qa-local is the canonical source |

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

In v25.8 a self-reference handling branch was added to `CreateParentData` (#2579, EPM-40619) to prevent a stack-overflow recursion in a recursive-rule scenario. Combined with the downstream `IsInCache`-based "PID reuse" heuristic, the new branch produces a **false-positive null return** when:

1. The process being evaluated has been EPM-tokenized (so its `Id()` resolves to itself in the token cache), and
2. Its parent is alive and EPM-tokenized (so the OS-found parent's token is in the cache too).

The null return inverts under `NegateCheck` recursive parent rules and produces a wrong block. The customer (HELP-13293, McKinsey) hit this with a "block PowerShell unless one of [Cursor.exe, ...] is in the parent chain" rule. When PowerShell ran scripts launched from Cursor, PowerShell's internal `__PSScriptPolicyTest_*.ps1` hosted-file probe re-evaluated the block rule on the now-EPM-tokenized PowerShell, the self-reference branch fired, and the block triggered incorrectly.

The "PID reuse" heuristic is misnamed — it doesn't actually require PID reuse, it fires whenever the OS-found parent has its token in the cache, which is the normal state for any rule-matched ancestor.

## Solution

Replace the in-line token-source resolution algorithm in `CreateParentData` with a call to `CPGProcessInfo::GetParentPidByToken`, which:

- Tries `Id()` first; if it resolves to self, falls through to `ParentId()`.
- Returns 0 when neither resolves, allowing the existing PID-based fallback to run.

`GetParentPidByToken` is the same algorithm already used in production by `CPGProcessInfo::GetParentPid()` and `InitializeProcessHandle()` — this is convergence onto the system's existing parent-resolution algorithm, not a new implementation. The function is promoted from private to public for cross-module reuse. No additional locking is required: the function reads `m_TokenSourceIdentifier` and `m_dwPid` (both treated as set-once-then-read by the class — `m_TokenSourceIdentifier` is already read unlocked from `GetTokenSourceIdentifier()` and other public methods) and calls into `TokenCache`, which is independently synchronized via its own internal mutex.

The fix:
- Eliminates the false-positive PID-reuse trip for the EPM-53842 case.
- Preserves the EPM-40619 stack-overflow protection — each recursion advances via `ParentId()` rather than self-looping.
- Keeps the real PID-reuse defence (`CreateParent(parentPid)`'s creation-time check at `PGInfoContainer.cpp:466`) on both cache-based and PID-fallback paths.
- Drops the `isBaseProcess` parameter (the load-bearing assumption that broke at depth 0) and the unused `recursionCount` parameter (incremented but never read).

A regression test `App Matching - Parent - NegateCheck recursive ancestor walk through EPM-tokenized chain` is added to `ParentProcess.feature` and a `WithControllingParentGroup` builder helper is added to `ApplicationBuilder` to support it. The scenario reproduces the customer's bug deterministically without requiring real PID reuse, and was confirmed to fail on `main` and pass on the fixed branch.

Replaces #3779 (Support team POC).

body:
## Problem

The `/test-plan` Claude Code skill was designed for a single-shot workflow: run it once against a Jira issue and ship the resulting Confluence page. Two gaps surfaced in feedback from a colleague:

- **No record of issue maturity at generation time.** A QA engineer reading a published test plan can't tell whether the underlying Jira issue had been through backlog refinement when the plan was written, or whether the AC / description was still being shaped. Plans generated against a sparse, pre-refinement issue look the same on the page as plans generated against a finalised one.
- **Update mode is PR-centric.** When the skill is re-run on the same issue, it enters update mode and appends new items it derives from a newly linked PR. But it doesn't treat changes to the **Jira issue itself** (richer description, finalised AC, clarified scope — typical outputs of backlog refinement) as a first-class signal. Additions are also always labelled `[Added from PR]`, which mis-attributes Jira-driven changes. And there's no mechanism for the case where refined AC means an *existing* test should be reworded — update mode is purely additive, and the \"never modify or remove existing content\" rule (which exists to protect QA edits to the page) prevents the skill from rewriting the test in place.

A colleague suggested using the skill before backlog refinement (to surface complex test environments and cross-team dependencies for the scrum team to discuss) as well as after it. Re-running was already supported at a mechanical level, but the skill's behaviour didn't fit the workflow well.

## Solution

All changes confined to [.claude/skills/test-plan/SKILL.md](.claude/skills/test-plan/SKILL.md). No code changes elsewhere.

- **Issue maturity classification** added in step 3, anchored on the team's confirmed EPM workflow: `New` → `Approved` (post triage / amigos) → `Ready` (post backlog refinement, \"selectable for a sprint\") → `In Progress` → `In Review` → `Ready for Merge` → `Done`. `Ready` and onwards is `finalised`; `New` / `Approved` is `pre-refinement`. Falls back to `statusCategory.key` for unfamiliar status names.
- **Status banner** added as element 2 of the page structure (after the TOC, before the Jira link). Yellow `warning` panel for pre-refinement issues, green `success` panel for finalised. Captures the actual status name so the reader sees it regardless. Designed as a snapshot — there's no implicit promise the skill will be re-run.
- **Update mode rewritten** so Jira and PR signals are peers. Step 5b's \"Identify what's new\" now re-derives the plan against the *current* Jira content and any linked PR, then compares against the existing page. This means a refinement-only refresh (no new PR linked) will correctly pick up new AC and surface new tests.
- **Source-specific provenance** for additions: `[Added from Jira]` / `[Added from PR]` / `[Added from refinement]` (when both / mixed). The `versionMessage` describes provenance per item.
- **Non-destructive `Refinement update suggested` mechanism**: when refined context implies an existing test should change, an ADF info panel (`panelType: \"note\"`) is appended directly *below* the existing test as a sibling — never modifying the test itself. QA decides whether to apply the suggestion.
- **One narrow exception** to the \"never modify or remove existing content\" rule: the new status banner may be *replaced* on re-run if `issue_maturity` has changed. Every other element on the page remains untouchable.
- **Update-mode reporting** expanded in step 7 to surface separate counts (added by source, update suggestions, banner refreshed) plus the existing \"no changes needed\" no-op case.

The change is purely additive in terms of existing behaviour: every existing rule (issue type validation, three-state customfield_10097 classification once EPM-54073 lands, page template, \"never modify\" core rule, link preservation, no-op re-runs) is preserved. The only difference users will see on the same input is that update-mode additions are now labelled with the more accurate source prefix.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Semgrep code-scanning alert [#2033](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/security/code-scanning/2033) (high severity, CWE-78) flags the `Upload to Artifactory` step in `.github/workflows/driver-build.yml` for shell injection. The step interpolates `${{ github.ref_name }}` and `${{ github.run_number }}` directly into a PowerShell `run:` block:

```yaml
run: |
  $refName = \"${{ github.ref_name }}\"
  $runNumber = \"${{ github.run_number }}\"
```

`github.ref_name` is the Git ref that triggered the workflow. Git allows branch names to contain double-quotes, semicolons, etc., so a branch named `release/foo\"; <pwsh>; \"` (which the `release/*` trigger would accept) breaks out of the double-quoted string and executes arbitrary PowerShell on the self-hosted driver-build runner — exposing `JFROG_ARTIFACTORY_VCPKG_TOKEN` and giving the attacker a foothold on a long-lived shared build machine. CVSS 4.0 = **8.7 High**.

## Solution

Move both interpolations into an `env:` block on the step and read them inside the script as `$env:REF_NAME` / `$env:RUN_NUMBER`. PowerShell's `$env:` access does not re-evaluate the value, so injection is impossible regardless of the ref name.

This mirrors the safe pattern already used by the `Resolve ticket number` step lower in the same file, and the [EPM-53820](https://beyondtrust.atlassian.net/browse/EPM-53820) fix that addressed the same Semgrep rule across three other workflows. `runner.temp` interpolation in the same step is left as-is — it's `runner` context (generated by the runner, not user input) and not flagged by the rule.

body:
## Problem

The `test-plan` skill's Jira-field update step could silently overwrite content the QA had typed into the Test Result and Evidence field. Step 4 distinguished only between \"no test plan link\" and \"existing test plan link\", leaving the case where the field already held *other* content (QA notes, prior test execution summaries, links to other docs) undefined. Step 6 then assumed the field was empty for new plan mode and wrote the link as the entire field value — destroying the existing notes.

## Solution

- **Step 4** now classifies the field into three explicit states:
  - **Empty** → new plan mode, write the link.
  - **Contains a Confluence test plan link** (URL points to a page under the Test Plans parent in PMFW, or matches the `{Issue Key} - … - Test Plan` title) → update mode, don't touch the field.
  - **Contains other content** → new plan mode (preserve), generate the plan but append the link below the existing content rather than overwriting.
- **Step 6** now branches on the classified state. The preserve case keeps the existing ADF intact, adds a separator paragraph, then appends the test plan link paragraph. The user is told in step 7 if the preserve path was taken, so they know existing notes were retained alongside the new link.

> Note: the single commit on this branch references `EPM-54073` in its message (the original ticket the skill was raised under). The PR title carries the correct ticket (`EPM-54213`); on squash merge the PR title becomes the commit message in main, so the wrong reference doesn't end up there.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

The `/crash-dump` Claude skill (in `.claude/skills/crash-dump/`) downloads matching DefendpointService PDB symbols for a build, then runs `cdb` to analyse a Windows crash dump. Its symbol-download step still pointed at Azure DevOps — `az pipelines runs artifact download` against the `_ServiceSymbols` artifact on FullBuild (722) / FeatureBuild (723), with a REST-API fallback for SSL flakiness.

EPM-W builds have moved to GitHub Actions, which publish `ServiceSymbols_<major>.<minor>.zip` to JFrog Artifactory under `eng-generic-{qa,dev}-local/epm-pmfw/client/<branch>/<version>/`. The skill's AzDo path no longer works against new builds, and we don't want backwards compat — once builds finish migrating, the AzDo lookup is dead weight.

## Solution

Replace Step 2 of the skill (symbol download) with a JFrog flow that mirrors the existing `/fetch-epm-installer` skill. Steps 1, 3, 4, 5 (dump validation, `cdb` analysis, follow-up commands, presenting findings) are unchanged.

Two files:

- **`.claude/skills/crash-dump/SKILL.md`** — Step 2 rewritten. All AzDo references gone (`az pipelines`, `dev.azure.com`, FullBuild/FeatureBuild definition IDs, REST fallback). Now points at the bundled helper script.
- **`.claude/skills/crash-dump/scripts/Get-EPMServiceSymbols.ps1`** — new helper. Searches both `eng-generic-qa-local` (main/release) and `eng-generic-dev-local` (other), filters Artifactory metadata properties (`product.version` for `-Version`, `github.run_id` for `-RunId`), then `jf rt curl`s just the per-arch nested zip out of the outer `ServiceSymbols_*.zip` via the archive-entry trick (`<zip>!/<entry>`) — same mechanism `Get-EPMInstaller.ps1` uses to avoid pulling the full bundle. The inner zip is then expanded locally to produce the PDBs.

**Identifier set:** `-Version` and `-RunId` only (deliberately narrower than `Get-EPMInstaller.ps1`'s full Version/RunId/Branch/Author/Sha set — symbol lookups in practice come from a dump's FileVersion or a CI run ID, not a branch).

**Real ARM64 finding:** the ARM64 inner zip ships only `DefendpointService.pdb` — `DefendpointBeyondInsightAdapter.pdb` and `PasswordSafeService.pdb` are x86/x64 only. Documented in SKILL.md so future ARM64 dump analysis doesn't trip on it.

**Validation:**

- Sanity-ran `Get-EPMServiceSymbols.ps1 -Version 26.2.1.250 -Arch x64` → 3 PDBs extracted: `DefendpointService.pdb` (87 MB), `DefendpointBeyondInsightAdapter.pdb` (24 MB), `PasswordSafeService.pdb` (18 MB).
- Ran 3 evals against the new SKILL.md via subagents (version-x64, runid-x64, version-arm64). All 3/3 passed assertions about PDB presence, correct script flags, and absence of any AzDo calls. Mean 41.9 s ± 2.5 s, ~38.7K tokens per run.

**Out of scope:** No backwards-compat for AzDo. No changes to `cdb` crash-analysis. No product code changes.

body:
## Problem

Downloading a single EPM installer from Artifactory — e.g. `PrivilegeManagementForWindows_x64.msi` for a specific build — currently requires pulling the full 740 MB `PMfW_*.zip` bundle. Devs end up waiting several minutes for a 60 MB file, or manually clicking around the JFrog web UI, which isn't scriptable from Claude Code.

## Solution

Add a Claude Code skill at `.claude/skills/fetch-epm-installer/` that:

- **Uses Artifactory's archive-entry REST API** (`<path-to-zip>!/<entry>`) to stream just the requested installer out of the zip — same mechanism the JFrog web UI uses when you click a file inside a zip. A 67 MB MSI downloads in ~7s instead of waiting on 740 MB.
- **Supports five ways to identify a build** — version (`26.2.1.10278`), GitHub run ID, branch name, author/actor, or commit SHA. The PowerShell script searches both `eng-generic-qa-local` (main/release) and `eng-generic-dev-local` (feature branches).
- **Scope is deliberately narrow** — only Client (`PrivilegeManagementForWindows`) and Policy Editor installers, x86/x64/ARM64 (where applicable) in MSI or EXE format. Response Generator, Agent Protection Utility, the ePO catalog, and symbol bundles are intentionally out of scope.
- **Rejects impossible variants up front** — e.g. Policy Editor has no ARM64, so the script errors before calling the API rather than silently failing.

`jf` CLI install + auth guidance lives in the skill's SKILL.md — if it's not set up, Claude walks the user through `winget install JFrog.JFrogCLI` and `jf login`.

### Alternatives considered

- **Full-bundle download + local unzip** — simplest but wasteful; ~10× more data transfer for most use cases.
- **HTTP Range + client-side ZIP central-directory parser** — works (one evaluation agent independently invented it) but ~3× slower and 50% more tokens than the archive-entry API, plus much more code to maintain.

## Problem

`ComputerGroupManager` had no unit test coverage, and its dependencies (`ITaskScheduler`, `IRegistryKey`, refresh task creation) were not injectable, making it difficult to test without real registry/network access.

## Solution

Refactored `ComputerGroupManager` to accept injected dependencies:
- `ITaskScheduler` replaces the previously embedded `icl::TaskScheduler<>` member
- `IRegistryKey` replaces the `RegistryKeyFlag` direct read for the feature flag, allowing tests to set the flag without touching the registry
- `TaskFactory` (`std::function<unique_ptr<ComputerGroupCacheRefreshTask>()>`) allows tests to inject a task backed by `MockNetApi32` to control domain-join behaviour

Production behaviour is preserved: `GetInstance()` uses an IIFE to open a real `CRegistryKey` at `PG_CLIENT_KEY` and passes a real `TaskScheduler<>`.

New test file `ComputerGroupManagerTests.cpp` covers 11 test cases across:
- `OnConfigLoad` with no filters (clears scheduler, does not stop thread)
- `OnConfigLoad` with filters and feature flag disabled (clears scheduler, does not stop thread)
- `OnConfigLoad` filters removed after previously being present
- `OnConfigLoad` called twice with no filters
- `OnConfigLoad` with filters and feature flag enabled — domain joined (registers task) and not domain joined (does not register)
- `OnConfigLoad` with no filters and feature flag enabled (clears scheduler)
- `Shutdown` (stops scheduler thread, does not clear task list)

The two \"FeatureFlagDisabled\" tests explicitly pass `MakeFeatureFlagRegistry(false)` so they fail loudly once the feature flag is removed, rather than silently passing with the feature enabled.

`MockTaskScheduler` gained a `stopAllCallCount` counter to allow asserting `Shutdown` does not clear the task list.

## Problem

The `Build Installers` job downloads `_BinariesAndSymbols_Temp` (~666 MB) at the start of every Full Build. On the InstallShield self-hosted runner, this download takes 7-20 min depending on network conditions, and sits squarely on the critical path of the build.

Most of those bytes are `.pdb` symbol files. The installers themselves do not need symbols — every `.ism` project file in the repo either does not reference `.pdb` at all, or references it in the `ExcludeFiles` column of the `ISDynamicFile` table (i.e. the installer is actively rejecting symbols at packaging time).

## Solution

Split the upload in `Finalise Builds` into two artifacts:

- `_Binaries_Temp` — same content as before, with `.pdb` files excluded
- `_Symbols_Temp` — only `.pdb` files, preserved as a separate GHA artifact for human or crash-dump access

`Build Installers` now downloads `_Binaries_Temp` instead of the combined artifact. The producer's existing `_ServiceSymbols` archive (curated production-grade subset) is unchanged.

No symbols are lost — they live in `_Symbols_Temp` instead of being bundled with the binaries.

Validated end-to-end on build [24836990836](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24836990836):

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Combined artifact size | 666 MB | 192 MB binaries + 493 MB symbols |
| Build Installers > Download binaries step | 452 s baseline (up to 20 min observed) | **162 s** |
| Smoke suites (PMfW Smoke + Insider Preview) | n/a | both passed |
| Symbols available to humans | combined artifact | `_Symbols_Temp` (493 MB) + `_ServiceSymbols` (70 MB, unchanged) |

Saves roughly 5 min off the critical path of every Full Build, with no symbol coverage loss.

A follow-up \"symbol coverage audit\" is worth doing separately to confirm that `_ServiceSymbols` covers every production binary that customer crash dumps need — but that's independent of this change and doesn't block it.

## Problem

Writing a test plan for each Jira issue is repetitive framing work — read the ticket, scan the codebase for affected areas, look up existing automation, decide regression scope, and manually assemble the standard Confluence template (Acceptance / Functional / Impact Area Regression / Integration / Compatibility / Automation / Security / Performance). Every ticket starts from a blank page.

## Solution

Adds a Claude Code skill, `/test-plan <issue-key>`, that produces an AI-generated draft test plan and publishes it to Confluence.

Files:
- `.claude/skills/test-plan/SKILL.md` — the skill definition

What it does end-to-end:
1. Fetches the Jira issue (summary, description, Acceptance Criteria, Implementation Notes; for Bugs also Reproduction Steps / Actual Result / Expected Result).
2. Validates issue type — only `Story`, `Bug`, `Vulnerability`, `Technical Debt` proceed.
3. Gathers additional context: parent epic for Stories; open PRs linked to the issue on `BeyondTrust/epm-windows` (full diff for small PRs, file list for large); relevant product code under `DefendpointService`/`PGHook`/`PGDriver`; existing SpecFlow feature files under `Tests/Automation`; Xray manual tests matching the issue's components.
4. Maps each impacted area to existing automation, so the plan says \"run this scenario\" rather than inventing duplicate regression tests.
5. Generates an ADF document following the standard test plan template and publishes it as a flat child of the \"Test Plans\" parent page in the PMFW space.
6. Writes the Confluence page link back into the Jira issue's Test Result and Evidence field.
7. On re-run against an issue that already has a plan (e.g. after a PR is linked), runs in **update mode**: fetches the existing page and appends only new items prefixed `[Added from PR]` — never modifies QA's existing content.

The skill encodes quality rules refined through review with QA:
- Scope awareness — only test the component actually changing
- Consistent Given/When/Then structure
- Prefer existing automation coverage over new regression tests
- Default OS is latest GA Windows 11 x64, with explicit deviation criteria (locale-specific bugs, server-side features, driver/kernel changes, legacy OS compat, Arm64-in-scope)
- Flag environment requirements (IPv6 network, locale OS, DC, etc.) that the current automation setup may not support

Output is always labelled as an AI-generated draft requiring QA review. The intent is to give QA a faster starting point, not replace their judgement.

body:
## Problem

PR #3757 (merged yesterday) silently changed the contract for the reusable test-suite workflow: **test failures no longer turn the GHA run red.** Only machine/infra errors do. The portal still reports the true pass/fail, but GitHub Actions reports the run as all green.

Example: [run 24810691324](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24810691324) conclusion is `success` across all 45 jobs, while [the portal report](https://portal.btrusteng.com/Reports/MainReport?BuildID=24810691324) shows failures.

### Why

PR #3757 addressed two failure modes that were causing `MemoryLeakStaging_*` artifacts to be dropped when a test suite failed. It shipped two fixes to the Factory-wrapper step:

1. `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` on the `Copy memory leak results` and `Upload memory leak staging` steps — runs them on both success and failure.
2. `$global:LASTEXITCODE = 0` inside the `$exitCode -eq 1` branch — clears Factory's \"some tests failed\" signal so PowerShell doesn't propagate it into the step's implicit exit code.

Only (1) was actually needed to preserve the artifacts. (2) is strictly redundant for the artifact goal, and its side effect was to flip the Factory step from red to green on test failure — which is what removed the test-failure signal from the GHA run.

### Coverage matrix

| Change                       | Tests failed (Factory exit 1)                 | Factory crashed (exit ≠ 0, 1)                 |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Neither (pre-#3757)          | step red, memory-leak steps **skipped** (lost) | step red, memory-leak steps **skipped** (lost) |
| Only `$LASTEXITCODE = 0`     | step green, memory-leak steps run             | step red, memory-leak steps **skipped** (lost) |
| Only `!cancelled()`          | step red, memory-leak steps run               | step red, memory-leak steps run               |
| Both (what #3757 shipped)    | **step green**, memory-leak steps run         | step red, memory-leak steps run               |

`!cancelled()` is strictly more robust than `$LASTEXITCODE = 0` — it preserves artifacts in both failure modes, whereas `$LASTEXITCODE = 0` alone still loses them when Factory crashes hard.

## Solution

Remove the `$global:LASTEXITCODE = 0` line (and the 4-line comment above it) from the `if ($exitCode -eq 1)` branch in `reusable-run-test-suite.yml`. The `Write-Host \"::warning::...\"` annotation is preserved so the run log still calls out the \"tests failed\" case.

After this change:

- Factory exit 0 → step succeeds ✓
- Factory exit 1 (tests failed) → step fails (red GHA) ✓, memory-leak steps still run via `!cancelled()` ✓
- Factory exit other (crash) → step fails (red GHA) ✓, memory-leak steps still run via `!cancelled()` ✓

### Alternatives considered

- **Leave `$LASTEXITCODE = 0` in place and add a separate terminal step that fails when `failed-tests == true`.** Would also work, but adds a new signal/output where removing one line gets the same behaviour. Rejected for churn.
- **Leave as-is and treat portal as source of truth for pass/fail.** Would require socialising the convention change with the team and updating any tooling/dashboards that watch GHA run colour. Out of proportion to the accidental scope of #3757.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

The crash-dump skill needs to download PDB symbols for a specific build version when triaging a `.dmp` file. Today, symbols only live on GitHub Actions (the `_ServiceSymbols` artifact). To fetch them by version, a tool has to:

1. Call the `find-build` GitHub action (workflow API calls + `_BuildVersion` artifact downloads) to resolve version → run-id, then
2. Hit the GitHub Actions artifacts API with that run-id to download the symbol artifact.

That's GHA-only — no way to use `jf rt download` directly. Anything outside the workflow context (a local skill, an oncall script) has to either reimplement find-build or shell out to `gh`.

GHA's 90-day artifact retention is a separate hard cliff — symbols for older releases simply aren't there.

## Solution

In the existing `Publish to Artifactory` job, download `_ServiceSymbols`, zip it as `ServiceSymbols_<short>.zip`, and upload alongside the installer bundle to the same `<repo>/epm-pmfw/client/<short>/<version>/` path. Picked up by the existing `jf rt upload \"*.zip\"` glob — no new step, no new credentials. The existing `jf rt set-props` call tags it with the same `github.*` props automatically.

One new prop: **`product.version`**. With it, any tool that has the JFrog CLI can resolve and download symbols for a version with two calls:

```
jf rt search \"*/epm-pmfw/client/*/*/ServiceSymbols_*.zip\" --props=\"product.version=26.2.1.10316\"
jf rt download <path-from-above>
```

No GitHub API, no find-build dependency, no 90-day cliff.

`build.timestamp` was considered but dropped — JFrog already records `created` on every file.
`commit.subject` was considered but dropped — not worth the sanitisation overhead and `gh api` round-trip.

Single-file change, +19 / -2.

### Validation

Validated end-to-end on a precursor branch run ([build 24783888716](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24783888716)):

- `ServiceSymbols_26.2.zip` (73 MB, 3 inner per-arch PDB zips) uploaded to `eng-generic-dev-local/epm-pmfw/client/perf--…/26.2.1.10316/`
- `set-props` completed for all 5 published files including the symbol bundle (JFrog log: `Done setting properties`)
- A separate `jf rt search --props=product.version=26.2.1.10316` test resolved and returned the right path in <4 s

### Alternatives considered

- **Symbols at a sibling `epm-pmfw/symbols/<short>/<version>/` path** instead of co-located with installers. Cleaner separation if lifecycle policies ever diverge. Rejected for now: requires a separate `set-props` call, complicates the existing pattern. Trivial to split later if retention diverges.
- **Per-PDB upload** instead of one bundled zip. Selective downloads, but more API calls. Crash-dump tooling needs the full symbol set anyway, so atomic bundle wins.

## Problem

The `@BIEventFolderFull` scenario fills the BeyondInsight events folder by calling `SysIO.File.Create()` 25,000 times but never disposes the returned `FileStream`s. The files stay locked by `testhost.x86.exe`, so the next scenario's `CreateEventsFolder` fails with:

> `IOException: The process cannot access the file 'dummyfile15144' because it is being used by another process`

This cascades: the dirty events folder causes `CreateFakeAdapter` in every subsequent `@UseFakeBIAdapter` feature's `BeforeFeature` to fail before `AddService` runs, which then makes `AfterFeature`'s `RemoveFakeAdapter` assert on a missing service — so `DeleteEventsFolder` never runs and the folder remains dirty for the rest of the run. One leaked handle bricks every downstream legacy-auditing test.

See [EPM-51539](https://beyondtrust.atlassian.net/browse/EPM-51539) for the originating failure.

## Solution

Wrap `SysIO.File.Create(...)` in a `using` block so each handle is released immediately:

```csharp
using (SysIO.File.Create(path + \"\dummyfile\" + i)) { }
```

The file is still created; we just don't keep the stream open. This is the minimal change — the existing try/catch, loop bounds, and error logging are untouched.

body:
## Problem

Two distinct failure modes were silently dropping `MemoryLeakStaging_*` workflow artifacts whenever a test suite failed. `auto-regression.yml` downloads those artifacts across all suites in a run and feeds them into `MemLeakAnalysis.exe` to detect unknown memory leaks — a suite whose files were dropped because its tests failed leaves the analysis incomplete and can mask real leaks.

**Failure mode 1 — Factory wrapper leaks `$LASTEXITCODE`.** The wrapper around `BeyondTrust.DevOps.Factory.exe` intends exit code 1 (\"some tests failed\") to be a `::warning::` that lets the step succeed so downstream copy/upload steps can run. But PowerShell preserves `$LASTEXITCODE` from the native exe into the script's implicit exit code, so the step fails anyway — and every subsequent step defaults to `if: success()` and gets skipped.

Example: [run 24698306838 / AppPrivMan](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24698306838) — Factory logs `View the test report here: …`, wrapper logs `##[warning]One or more machines have failed tests`, step still ends `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1`.

**Failure mode 2 — Copy/Upload steps default to `success()` gating.** Even when Factory itself crashes (exit code other than 0/1) or when the now-removed `Copy test results locally` hit a vstest-scratch-file enumeration race on `\fs01\ExecutionProduction\…\Artefacts\<guid>`, the memory-leak Copy/Upload steps would be skipped as a cascade, losing the data we actually wanted.

**Evidence (14-day sample):**

| Run | Date | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| [24698306838](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24698306838) | 2026-04-21 (scheduled) | ~16 suites dropped `MemoryLeakStaging_*` |
| [24643511667](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24643511667) | 2026-04-20 (scheduled) | ~16 suites dropped `MemoryLeakStaging_*` |
| [24688748454](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24688748454) | 2026-04-20 | all 5 TAP soak slices dropped |

## Solution

Three small changes in `reusable-run-test-suite.yml`:

1. **Fix the wrapper exit-code leak.** After the `$exitCode -eq 1` warning branch, set `$global:LASTEXITCODE = 0` so PowerShell doesn't propagate Factory's `1` into the step's implicit exit code. The step now succeeds on tests-only-failed (which is the intended behaviour).

2. **`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`** on `Copy memory leak results` and `Upload memory leak staging`. Runs them on success **and** failure, but still skips on explicit job cancellation — where the test VM may be mid-operation and copying could hang. Chosen over `always()` for that cancel-safety.

3. **Defensively handle empty `base-directory` output.** If Factory crashes before writing its step output, the copy step now exits `0` with a `::warning::` rather than failing on an invalid path.

## Also deleted

**`Copy test results locally` and `Upload test results`** — the `TestResults_*.trx` artifact had **no consumer** (no `download-artifact` reference anywhere in the repo, no test-reporter action, no external pull). The equivalent info will land in the portal. Removing it also dodges a `Copy-Item -Recurse` race on vstest scratch files under `\fs01\…\Artefacts\<guid>` that was independently failing the step when the tests themselves had succeeded.

**Alternatives considered:**
- `if: always()` — runs on cancellation too, risks hanging on a mid-operation test VM. `!cancelled()` is the safer equivalent.
- Adding `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` to the recursive `Copy-Item` — only needed because of the `TestResults_*.trx` upload path; moot once that upload is removed.
- Leaving the `TestResults_*.trx` upload in place for transitional safety — but uploading an artifact no one downloads costs storage and obscures intent. Cleaner to drop it.

body:
## Problem

Unit test runs on GitHub Actions intermittently fail with `The active test run was aborted. Reason: Test host process crashed`, at roughly 14% per-run on CI (and ~100% locally against some test sets). The failures started when we migrated from AzDO; the same self-hosted runners were fine on AzDO, but the GitHub Actions pipeline added `/Collect:\"Code Coverage;Format=Xml\"` to `vstest.console.exe`.

Root cause: Microsoft Code Coverage's **dynamic native instrumentation** patches code at runtime in already-loaded DLLs to insert coverage probes. The patching perturbs SEH unwind tables in instrumented functions, so C++ exceptions occasionally fail to match their catch handlers and escape up into testhost, terminating the process. Microsoft documented this class of issue and, in .NET 10, changed the default to disable dynamic native instrumentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/compatibility/sdk/10.0/code-coverage-dynamic-native-instrumentation

## Solution

Switch the collector to **static** native instrumentation (patches binaries on disk before tests run), and disable dynamic instrumentation entirely. Three pieces:

1. **`Build/unit-tests.config.xml`** — vstest `/Settings:` file, taken from Microsoft's published Code Coverage sample. Deviations from upstream:
   - `<EnableDynamicNativeInstrumentation>False</…>` (was True) — eliminates the testhost-crash trigger. Empirically measured: coverage numbers identical to Dynamic=True (see below), so there's no tradeoff.
   - `<Format>Xml</Format>` (was `coverage`) — matches what we actually want from this pipeline.
   - `<IncludeTestAssembly>False</…>` (was True) — coverage of production code only; test DLLs were already excluded at the Sonar side.
   - Placeholders/Fabrikam examples removed.
   - Filename is not `*.runsettings` to dodge a repo push-protection rule on that extension; vstest accepts any XML path.

2. **`CommonProperties.props`** — add `/PROFILE` to the linker for `*Tests` projects. Static instrumentation requires `/PROFILE`. Scoped to `*Tests` via `MSBuildProjectName` so ship binaries stay byte-identical (ICF folding stays on for non-test projects).

3. **`reusable-client-build.yml`** — pass `/Settings:` to `vstest.console.exe`, and bump `Microsoft.TestPlatform` from 17.14.1 to 18.4.0 (pulled from Jack's `jl/unit-test-runsettings`; not strictly required but keeps us current).

### Alternatives considered and discarded
- Keeping `EnableDynamicNativeInstrumentation=True` to match the MS sample — initial attempt, reduced crash rate but didn't eliminate it (1 crash in 5 runs) because production DLLs without `/PROFILE` still got dynamically instrumented. Coverage measurements showed zero benefit to keeping Dynamic=True, so it was dropped.
- Dropping code coverage in CI — loses SonarQube data; not acceptable.
- Adding `/PROFILE` to production projects — not needed once Dynamic is off; would also affect ship binaries (loses ICF folding).
- Refactoring the production C++ code that throws the offending exceptions — way out of scope and treats the symptom, not the collector bug.

### Verification

**Crash rate:** 27/27 ReleaseStatic x64 CI runs clean with Dynamic=False (24/24 at the original `11820b0cf` validation + 3/3 on this branch at `991c21a75`). Pre-fix baseline was ~14% crashes on CI. With the intermediate Dynamic=True variant we still saw 1/5 crashes on this branch.

**Coverage:** Static Analysis run `24774632484` (commit `991c21a75`, Dynamic=False) shows the same coverage as the Dynamic=True run before it:

| Project | Dynamic=False | Dynamic=True (prior) |
|---|---|---|
| defendpoint-release | 68.6% | 68.6% |
| defendpoint-releasestatic | 60.7% | 60.7% |

All three Sonar projects (driver, release, releasestatic) successfully consumed the vscoveragexml reports.

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

`DefendpointServiceLib/DefendpointService.cpp::ProcessPMCPolicyUpdate` forwarded arbitrary JSON supplied by any caller over the SYSTEM service pipe straight to the PMC Adapter's named pipe. Because the service pipe DACL grants Authenticated Users access, any local user could proxy crafted PMC policy-update requests through the service to the cloud management channel — potentially triggering unintended cloud operations or learning PMC Adapter response details.

Tracked in [EPM-53340](https://beyondtrust.atlassian.net/browse/EPM-53340).

The earlier attempt at this (PR #3745, now closed) only added a `MessageSecurityChecker` sender gate. That restricted *who* could proxy, but the payload remained fully caller-controlled — the service was still a generic JSON passthrough.

## Solution

Move the entire PMC force-policy exchange into the service. EndpointUtility and SystemTray now send nothing but a `PGMsgPMCPolicyUpdate` signal; the service constructs the `ForcePolicyUpdate` request, sends it to the PMC Adapter, parses the response, and returns the final user-facing result string (`Updated`, `NoUpdates`, `ParseError`, or `ADAPTER_ERROR`). The client only knows how to emit `DEFENDPOINT_ERROR` when it cannot reach the service.

Concretely:

- `DefendpointService.cpp::ProcessPMCPolicyUpdate` builds the request via `JsonRequestHandler::BuildRequestAsJson(Request<pmc::RequestHeader>{{PMCRequestId::ForcePolicyUpdate}})`, parses the PMC reply with `pmc_response_handler::force_policy::ParseJsonResponse`, and writes the resolved status string to `PG_REPLY_PMC_POLICY_UPDATE_RESPONSE`.
- `CloudCommunicationsLib/PMCConnection.cpp::detail::ExecuteForcePolicy` shrinks to \"send `PGMsgPMCPolicyUpdate`, return the result string from the reply (or `DEFENDPOINT_ERROR` on pipe failure)\".
- `PG_MSG_PMC_POLICY_UPDATE_REQUEST` retired from `PGMessageDefinitions.h` — no longer sent on the wire.
- Unused `pmc_policy_update_results::RequestError` constant removed.
- `MessageSecurityChecker` sender gate (EndpointUtility or TaskTray) kept at handler entry as defense in depth.

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

The PMfW smoke workflow has two artifact-download pain points:

- **Failing reliability on `Download PMC artifacts`**: the step intermittently fails after ~25 minutes with `An existing connection was forcibly closed by the remote host` when pulling from Azure DevOps. Root cause: Windows PowerShell 5.1's `Invoke-WebRequest` is slow for binary downloads (synchronous, buffered, progress bar active), and AzDO's `/artifacts?$format=zip` endpoint closes slow/idle connections on large artifacts. The self-hosted runner image (`gha-shr-base` / `factory-gha`) does not ship `pwsh`, so switching shell is not an option.
- **Slow `Download installers from Artifactory`**: takes ~5 minutes to pull a single PMfW bundle from JFrog because `jf rt download` defaults to only 5 parallel byte-ranges per file, which throttles single-file downloads.

## Solution

- **Reliability fix**: replace `Invoke-WebRequest` with `System.Net.WebClient.DownloadFile` in the `download-pmc-artifacts` action for both `AdapterInstallers` and `PackageManagerInstaller` downloads, wrapped in a 3-attempt retry with linear backoff (5s after attempt 1, 10s after attempt 2). `WebClient` streams to disk rather than buffering and is ~10× faster on PS 5.1; the retry absorbs transient AzDO connection resets.
- **Opportunistic speed-up**: `$ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'` added to the remaining PowerShell steps using `Invoke-WebRequest` (`reusable-client-build`, `reusable-driver-build`, `dependency-vulnerability-analysis`, `find-build`). Pure speed bump, zero behaviour change.
- **JFrog parallelisation**: `jf rt download` bumped from the default `--split-count=5` to `--split-count=15 --threads=8` for the installer bundle. For a single large file, `--split-count` controls how many byte-range chunks are pulled in parallel.

### Validated on run [24719995694](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/actions/runs/24719995694)

| Step | Baseline | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Download installers from Artifactory | 287s | **130s** (55% faster) |
| Download PMC artifacts | timed out at ~25min | **52s** (single attempt, no retry needed) |

### Alternatives considered
- **Switch shell to `pwsh`**: ruled out. The runner image is Windows Server Core 2022 with no `pwsh` installed; would need a base-image rebuild.
- **`az pipelines runs artifact download` instead of direct AzDO API**: larger refactor, same underlying HTTP behaviour, extra tool dependency.
- **Parallelising steps 5-8** (`_ServiceSymbols`, `_Automation*`, `_AutoInfrastructure`): would save ~2.5 min, but requires replacing `actions/download-artifact@v8` with bespoke PowerShell. Out of scope for this PR; candidate for a follow-up.
- **Bundling `_ServiceSymbols` / `_Automation*` into one artifact at publish time**: bigger structural change, also a candidate follow-up.

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

The `ChallengeAuth` and `ChallengeORAuth` automation tests were highly flaky on `main`. Analysis of the last 7 runs (2026-03-13 to 2026-04-13) showed challenge-response tests failing on **43–71% of runs** across the AppControlAuth suite (52 affected tests).

The root cause is in `EnterAResponseCodeIntoThePopupFromTheCmdLine`:

1. **No focus guard before entering the response code.** After `PGChallengeResponse.exe` runs and exits, the challenge popup may no longer be in the foreground. Entering the response code without first focusing the window causes keystrokes to go to the wrong window, silently producing an incorrect code or no input at all.
2. **No assertion that `PGChallengeResponse.exe` ran successfully.** `ProcessRunner.RunAndWaitAsync` swallows launch exceptions and returns `false` with `ExitCode = 0`. Without a guard, a silent launch failure causes response code `0` to be entered into the popup, failing at a downstream step with a misleading error message.

## Solution

Two targeted changes to `EnterAResponseCodeIntoThePopupFromTheCmdLine`:

1. Added `Assert.IsTrue(task.Result, $"PGChallengeResponse.exe failed to run: {runner.LaunchError}")` — fails fast with a clear diagnostic if the process did not launch, rather than silently using response code `0`.
2. Added `DefendpointMessage.Window.Focus()` after confirming the popup is still visible — ensures the popup window is in the foreground before entering the response code, guarding against focus loss after the external process exits.

A third change adds a direct `FlaUI.Core` assembly reference to `BeyondTrust.Automation.Windows.Bindings.Common.csproj` (and its `packages.config`). <!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Semgrep flagged three high-severity shell-injection findings (CWE-78) in our GitHub Actions workflows. Each one uses `${{ ... }}` context expressions — including user-controllable `workflow_dispatch` inputs — directly inside a `run:` block, so a crafted input could inject arbitrary shell/PowerShell into the runner.

- `ansible.yml` — [alert 1993](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/security/code-scanning/1993): `${{ inputs.playbook }}` interpolated into the `ansible-playbook` command.
- `reusable-client-build.yml` — [alert 2030](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/security/code-scanning/2030): `${{ runner.temp }}`, `${{ inputs.build-configuration }}`, and `${{ inputs.build-platform }}` interpolated into the `msbuild /bl:` path.
- `create_release_branch.yml` — [alert 2012](https://github.com/BeyondTrust/epm-windows/security/code-scanning/2012): `${{ env.release_branch }}` and `${{ github.event.inputs.jira_ticket }}` interpolated into a `gh workflow run` call.

## Solution

Apply the standard mitigation called out by both Semgrep and GitHub's [script-injection hardening guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/learn-github-actions/security-hardening-for-github-actions#understanding-the-risk-of-script-injections): move each `${{ ... }}` expression into an `env:` binding on the step and reference it via a shell variable in the `run:` body.

- `ansible.yml` — add `PLAYBOOK: ${{ inputs.playbook }}` and use `\"${PLAYBOOK}.yml\"`.
- `create_release_branch.yml` — add `RELEASE_BRANCH` and `JIRA_TICKET` env bindings and reference them as `\"$RELEASE_BRANCH\"` / `\"$JIRA_TICKET\"`.
- `reusable-client-build.yml` — reuse the existing `BUILD_CONFIGURATION` / `BUILD_PLATFORM` env bindings as `$env:BUILD_CONFIGURATION` / `$env:BUILD_PLATFORM`, and swap `${{ runner.temp }}` for the built-in `$env:RUNNER_TEMP`.

No behavioural change — the commands still run with the same values, just sourced safely from the environment.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

There was no guard to avoid starting the scheduled task when the feature is unused — wasting AD queries on endpoints where no `DeviceAccountsFilter` workstyle filters are configured.

## Solution

`ComputerGroupManager` now exposes an `OnConfigLoad()` method that checks whether any `DeviceAccountsFilterWindows` filters (`PGFilterTypeDeviceAccount`) exist across all loaded config sources, and calls `Initialize()` or `Clear()` accordingly. This is called from `LoadConfigurationAndStore` in `PGServiceConfig.cpp` after each config source is stored, following the same pattern as agent protection.

Key changes:
- `ComputerGroupManager::OnConfigLoad()` — new public method; encapsulates the policy check and init/clear decision
- `ComputerGroupManager::HasComputerGroupFilters()` — new private member; iterates all loaded configs via `g_ConfigurationManager.GetRetriever(nullptr)` to find any `PGFilterTypeDeviceAccount` filter
- `ComputerGroupManager::Initialize()` — guarded with `m_isInitialized` to prevent double-registration across multiple config source loads; feature flag check clears any running task when disabled
- `ComputerGroupManager::Shutdown()` — resets `m_isInitialized` before stopping the task scheduler thread
- `ComputerGroupManager::InitializeLocked()` — private helper containing the real init logic; all three public mutating methods (`Initialize`, `Shutdown`, `OnConfigLoad`) hold `m_mutex` before calling it or touching shared state, preventing races between concurrent config watcher and web policy threads
- Removed the unconditional `Initialize()` call from `DefendpointService::ServerThreadBody`

## Problem

`IdentityCheckSkippedForMFA_DifferentUser_ChildApp` (PMfW Regression - IdentityCore) has been flaky at ~27%, on the same ARM64 25H2 machine as the sibling scenario (EPM-53691). Failure logs from build 344401:

- Failing step is `Then the OIDC authentication completes` → `Assert.IsTrue failed` after **60.8 s** in `IdPBindings.TheMfaMessageIsAuthenticated()`. `HasIdPAuthCompleted()` gives up polling for the `\"Authenticated\"` marker after its `Retry.WhileNull` 60 s timeout.
- Screenshot differs from the sibling scenario: two Edge tabs are open. Tab 1 is still \"Loading…\" on `localhost:44321/connect/authorize?...`; Tab 2 shows `localhost:44322/?code=A0B0E3B0...` — the **OIDC server redirected with the auth code already**. The code was issued; the PMfW notification just hadn't rendered the \"Authenticated\" marker inside 60 s.

This is a slower warm-path / tab-split flake on first auth on a fresh ARM64 runner, not a purely environmental Edge block like EPM-53691. Complementary to that fix.

## Solution

Bump the `HasIdPAuthCompleted` `Retry.WhileNull` timeout from **60 s → 120 s** in `Framework/Defendpoint/NotificationPopup.cs`. Smallest change that gives the detection loop enough patience for the case where the callback did arrive but the notification UI took extra time to update on this runner.

If the two-tab split seen in the screenshot is actually a real browser-launch-path bug (wrong default browser + redirect to new tab), a longer poll just reduces flake rate without fixing the underlying race — worth a follow-up.

Freshly provisioned automation machines (observed on ARM64 Windows 11 25H2) open Microsoft Edge's first-run welcome page instead of the OIDC authorize URL when `DefendpointService` launches a browser for MFA. ## Problem

`CloneAndExecuteASQLDatabaseApplicationBuiltUsingCAndMSBuild` (PMfW Regression - Personas) has been flaky. Failure logs from build 343056 show **three** machines (`B-11-23H2-02`, `B-11-24H2-01`, `B-11-25H2-01`) all failing the same step with:

\`\`\`
CommonFrameworkException: Timeout after 30mins of winget cmd
  'install --manifest \"\fs01...\Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools\17.14.27\"
   --silent --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements
   --override \"--passive --wait --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Workload.ManagedDesktopBuildTools;includeRecommended\"'
\`\`\`

Durations: 30m 54s / 30m 58s / 30m 58s — right at the timeout wall. The preceding `Git.Git` install succeeded. <!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Following the Azure DevOps → GitHub Actions migration, all EPM-Windows test workflows that dispatch to self-hosted DevOps-IaC runners hardcoded `runs-on: [self-hosted, factory]`. There is no way for a dispatcher to choose which pool a run should target (production vs staging) or to pin to a custom label for bring-up/verification of new runners.

Affected workflows:
- `.github/workflows/reusable-run-test-suite.yml`
- `.github/workflows/run-test-suite.yml`
- `.github/workflows/auto-regression.yml` (including its `analysis` job)
- `.github/workflows/build.yml` (Full Build + post-build smokes)

## Solution

- Added a `devops-iac-runner-label` input to `reusable-run-test-suite.yml` (default `devops-iac-production`) and replaced the hardcoded `factory` label with `runs-on: [self-hosted, \"${{ inputs.devops-iac-runner-label }}\"]`.
- Exposed a matching `devops-iac-runner-label` `workflow_dispatch` input (plain text field, pre-populated with `devops-iac-production`) on `run-test-suite.yml`, `auto-regression.yml`, and `build.yml`, so dispatchers of any of the three top-level workflows can pick the pool.
- Plumbed the value through to the reusable workflow with a `|| 'devops-iac-production'` fallback, so scheduled / push-triggered runs (where dispatch inputs are empty) always land on production.
- Updated the `analysis` job in `auto-regression.yml` to honour the same resolved label rather than its own hardcoded `factory`.
- Chose a text input over a dropdown+custom pair: engineers working on DevOps-IaC know the exact label they want, and CI always hits `devops-iac-production` via the default — the dropdown added friction without value.

**Rollout note**: DevOps-IaC runners must be re-deployed with both the existing `factory` label and the new `devops-iac-{environment}` labels **prior to merge**, so jobs already in flight can still match a runner. After merge, `factory` can be removed from runners.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

We've seen intermittent `testhost.exe` crashes on the `ReleaseStatic x64` unit test job (exception code `0xE3530001` — `CppUnitTestFramework::CSEException`) at varying tests. We don't have dumps to analyse because no crash handler is registered on the build agents, so the process exits with no diagnostic artefact.

## Solution

New Ansible playbook `install-procdump.yml` targeting the `clientpr` + `clientbuild` host groups. It:

1. Creates `C:\dumps`
2. Downloads procdump from Sysinternals and extracts it into `C:\dumps`
3. Registers procdump as the AeDebug postmortem debugger (both 32-bit and 64-bit entries) with `-ma` so full dumps are written to `C:\dumps` on any crash

Also adds `install-procdump` to the ansible workflow's playbook dropdown so it can be run from GitHub Actions.

Scope intentionally limited to client build/PR agents for now — can extend to other pools later if useful.

## Problem

The `run-smokes` job in the full build workflow was gated on `build-installers` completing. <!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Our AzDO build pipeline captures an MSBuild binary log (`.binlog`) for every matrix cell of the `PrivilegeGuard.sln` build and publishes them as artifacts. They're the input to build-performance analysis via the `binlog-analysis` skill / MSBuild Structured Log Viewer.

The new GitHub Actions client build workflow (`.github/workflows/reusable-client-build.yml`) currently runs `msbuild` with no `/bl` flag, so no binlogs are produced. Perf work on GHA builds has no data to analyse.

## Solution

In `.github/workflows/reusable-client-build.yml`:

- Append `/bl:` to the standard `msbuild` command, writing to `${{ runner.temp }}\PrivilegeGuard_<config>_<platform>.binlog` so it stays out of the workspace and can't be pulled into unrelated artifacts.
- Skip `/bl` on the sonar build-wrapper path — the instrumentation distorts timings so those binlogs would be misleading for perf work.
- Add an `actions/upload-artifact` step gated on `inputs.mode == 'full-build' && !inputs.enable-static-analysis`, uploading one `_Binlog_<config>_<platform>` artifact per matrix cell (follows the existing `_Temp_<config>_<platform>` naming convention). PR CI and sonar runs therefore don't produce binlog artifacts.

Storage target is GitHub Actions artifacts, not Artifactory — binlogs are short-lived, single-build, single-purpose, and the run-scoped GHA artifact store fits cleanly.

Scope is client build only, matching the AzDO binlog coverage. The driver and automation builds never captured binlogs in AzDO either, so they're out of scope here.

## Summary

- In `IsKeyBlockedForWrite` (`PGDriver/AgentProtectionRegFilter.cpp:197`), the buffer size for a registry key path was computed by casting a ULONG sum to USHORT: `(USHORT)(rootKeyLength + keyName->Length + sizeof(L\"\\\") + sizeof(KEY_NAME_INFORMATION))`
- For deeply-nested registry keys, `rootKeyLength` (a ULONG from `ZwQueryKey`) can exceed 65535, causing the USHORT cast to truncate the allocation size
- `ExAllocatePoolWithTag` would allocate a too-small buffer while the subsequent `ZwQueryKey` used the original ULONG length, writing past the end of the allocation and corrupting the kernel NonPagedPool
- ~~This is exploitable from a standard user account to achieve kernel-mode code execution~~ Causes a BSOD, but no arbitrary execution

## Changes

- Changed `absoluteKeyLength` from `USHORT` to `ULONG`
- Used `RtlULongAdd` (overflow-checked addition) to compute the sum; returns false if any addition overflows or the total exceeds `MAXUSHORT`
- We now check the registry path does not exceed `USHORT`.
- Use a different variable to make the allocation, ensuring we support the win32 limit fully, but prevent the allocation bug.
- Added missing `ZwClose(rootKey)` calls on the two early-return paths that previously leaked the handle

## Test plan

- [x] Build PGDriver in ReleaseStatic x64 and verify no new warnings
- [x] Manual test: create a deeply-nested registry key hierarchy (128+ levels with 255-char names) and confirm the agent protection filter handles it without a system crash
- [x] Code review of the fix

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Conventional commit prefix rules were duplicated across several places in the repo:

- `README.md` inlined the list of allowed prefixes
- `.github/workflows/github-pr-validation-and-actions.yml` enforces the regex
- `.claude/skills/create-pr/SKILL.md` told Claude to read the workflow regex
- The canonical [Conventional Commits Confluence page](https://beyondtrust.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PMFW/pages/74449357/Conventional+Commits) documents the semantic meaning of each prefix

Claude frequently picked the wrong prefix when creating PRs (e.g. `chore` where `fix` was correct) because the semantic rules only lived on Confluence, which Claude does not read. The workflow regex validates the syntactic set of allowed types, not which one fits the change.

## Solution

- Added a \"Choosing the right type\" section to `.claude/skills/create-pr/SKILL.md` with a one-liner per prefix plus tie-breaker rules, sourced from the Confluence page, with a link back as the canonical source.
- Trimmed the `README.md` contributing bullet so it links to the Confluence page instead of duplicating the prefix list inline.
- Workflow regex left untouched — it remains the authoritative list of allowed prefixes.

Tradeoff considered: fetching the Confluence page at PR creation time would eliminate drift risk but adds latency, token cost, and an auth/network failure mode for rules that rarely change. The link in the skill lets reviewers spot drift.
