body:
## Problem

`CPGHostedFileHelper::GetPowerShellFile` diverges from PowerShell's documented command-line parsing in two related ways.

**1. Functional bug (EPM-34169).** Unknown `-xxx` tokens after a captured script path were treated as fatal "invalid switches", wiping the filename. A policy for `foo.ps1` fails to match:

```
powershell.exe -File C:\scripts\foo.ps1 -env some_env_name
```

**2. Privilege-escalation vector (found during review).** The parser also kept processing *whitelisted* engine switches (`-File`, `-Command`, ...) after a script path was captured, violating PowerShell's [documented rule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_powershell_exe?view=powershell-5.1#:~:text=All%20values%20typed%20after%20the%20File%20parameter%20are%20interpreted%20as%20the%20script%20filepath%20and%20parameters%20passed%20to%20that%20script) that *"File must be the last parameter... all values typed after the File parameter are interpreted as the script filepath and parameters passed to that script."* A crafted command line could report a different `.ps1` than what runs:

```
powershell.exe -File C:\Temp\evil.ps1 -File C:\Scripts\trusted.ps1
```

PowerShell runs `evil.ps1`; the old parser reported `trusted.ps1`, so an elevation rule for `trusted.ps1` would elevate `evil.ps1`.

## Solution

Align the parser with PowerShell's rule: once the script path is captured, every remaining token is a script argument. Added `strFilename.IsEmpty()` to the outer `for`-loop condition so the state machine exits immediately on capture — no further engine-switch processing, no re-entry into `PS_ExpectingFilenameNext` / `PS_ParseCommand`. Unknown switches *before* capture still invalidate (original safety preserved).

New unit tests cover the functional fix and each escalation variant:
- `-File` after `-File` (crafted evil/trusted path override)
- `-File` after positional script path
- `-Command "& 'x.ps1'"` after capture
- Parameterised tests: each `PS_SkipNextParm` switch (`-PSConsoleFile`, `-Version`, `-InputFormat`, `-OutputFormat`, `-WindowStyle`, `-EncodedCommand`, `-ExecutionPolicy`) and each single-form switch (`-NoLogo`, `-NoProfile`, `-NonInteractive`, `-Mta`, `-Sta`) appearing as a script argument after a captured filename.

New acceptance scenario in `AllowExecution.feature` exercises the customer repro end-to-end and checks the audit event preserves `-env some_env_name` in `process.command_line`.

## Problem

The `azdo-build` and `azdo-test` Claude skills reference Azure DevOps pipelines (FeatureBuild 723, FullBuild 722, RunTestSuite 730, RunRegression 729) that are being retired as CI/CD migrates to GitHub Actions.

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d273e83-75db-41fc-9fcb-4dd8ca6f1599

A race condition exists where `CPGRulesEngine::Find*()` methods iterate configurations via smart pointers, find a match, and return raw pointers into the configuration. The smart pointer goes out of scope when the method returns, so a concurrent config reload (BeyondInsight sync, GPO refresh, PMC push, local file change) can free the configuration while callers still hold raw pointers — causing STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION (0xc0000374).

PR #3081 partially mitigated this with a `ppConfiguration` out-parameter, but only 2 of ~15 callers used it. PR #3508 extended the same out-parameter to the three `PGServiceControl.cpp` sites that reproduced the customer crash, but left the remaining ~10 call sites exposed (including `UninstallerMatches`, `FindGeneralRule`, `IsJITAdminEnabled`, and the shell-extension / ActiveX / content-file paths). The out-parameter approach was also fragile — every new caller had to remember to pass it.

## Solution

Move config-lifetime management into the engine itself instead of pushing it onto every caller. On a match, each `Find*` / `UninstallerMatches` / `FindGeneralRule` / `IsJITAdminEnabled` method `std::move`s the matched configuration into a `mutable` member vector (`m_matchedConfigurations`), keeping it alive for the engine's lifetime. Since the engine is always stack-allocated per-request (or held as a member of a stack-allocated object like `ComRulesProcessor`), the config outlives all raw pointer usage.

This eliminates the bug class at the source rather than at each call site:
- **8 engine methods updated** to push the matched config into `m_matchedConfigurations` before returning: `FindApplicationToken`, `FindApplicationTokenById`, `FindCOMClassToken`, `FindAppxPackageToken`, `FindContentToken`, `UninstallerMatches`, `FindGeneralRule`, `IsJITAdminEnabled`.
- **`ppConfiguration` out-parameter removed** from `FindApplicationToken`, `FindApplicationTokenById`, and `ProcessCOMLaunchedRules` — now redundant.
- **`FindContentMatch` refactored** to take `CPGRulesEngine&` from the caller so the engine outlives the returned raw pointers; `FindRunAsUserMatch` similarly uses a caller-owned `std::optional<CPGRulesEngine>`.
- **All call sites** reordered so raw-pointer variables are declared after the engine and cannot outlive it.

Supersedes PR #3508.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Path-filtered PR workflows that are required status checks stay permanently pending when irrelevant files change, blocking merge. This is a known GitHub Actions limitation — when a workflow doesn't trigger (due to `on.pull_request.paths`), its checks are never reported.

## Solution

Replace path filtering on `pull_request` triggers with runtime path detection using `tj-actions/changed-files`. Each PR workflow now:

1. **Always triggers** on every PR (no `paths:` filter on `pull_request`)
2. **`Check paths` job** — always runs on ubuntu-latest (~10s). On pull_request, uses `tj-actions/changed-files` to detect relevant file changes. On any other trigger (push, schedule, etc.), outputs `should-run=true` automatically.
3. **Build jobs** — gated with `if: needs.changes.outputs.should-run == 'true'`, skipped when paths don't match
4. **Status gate job** (`<Name> Check`) — runs with `if: !cancelled()`, fails if changes or build jobs failed, passes when builds are skipped

When a job is skipped via `if:`, GitHub reports it as \"Success\" — so the required check passes without blocking.

Push triggers retain their path filters on the workflow trigger level (not required checks, no issue).

**Required check names for the ruleset:**
- `Client PR Check`
- `Driver PR Check`
- `Automation CI Check`
- `Endpoint App CI Check`
- `PowerRules CI Check`

## Problem

The Full Build pipeline always uses the pinned `DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER`. In AzDO, the `DriverVersionOption` parameter allowed choosing between the pinned version, the latest driver build on the branch, or triggering a fresh driver rebuild. This flexibility is missing in GitHub Actions.

## Solution

Add a `driver-version` choice input to `build.yml` with three options:

- **pinned** (default): Uses `DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER` env var — current behavior, no change for push/schedule triggers
- **latest**: Resolves the latest successful `driver-build.yml` run on the current branch via `actions/github-script` in the `finalise-builds` job
- **rebuild**: Triggers `driver-build.yml` in the `setup` job (runs in parallel with client builds), then waits for completion in `finalise-builds` using `actions/github-script` polling before downloading artifacts

The driver run number resolution uses a fallback chain: `steps.driver-rebuild.outputs.run-number || steps.driver-latest.outputs.run-number || env.DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER`

body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

The HKLM prefix check added in #3620 broke Agent Protection registry blocking for WOW64 (32-bit) registry paths on older OSes (LTSB 2016, Server 2012 R2, Server 2016).

When a 32-bit registry view access occurs on these OSes, `ObOpenObjectByPointer` succeeds on the `\REGISTRY` root object (instead of failing as the old comment assumed). The code then builds the absolute path as `root + "\" + CompleteName`, producing a malformed path like `\REGISTRY\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Avecto\Privilege Guard Client`. This double-prefixed path fails the `UnicodeStringStartsWith(\REGISTRY\MACHINE\)` check, so the write is allowed through.

The old code (before #3620) didn't have the HKLM prefix check, so `UnicodeStringFind` substring matching tolerated the malformed path. #3620 exposed a latent bug in the path construction.

## Solution

Per the [MSDN documentation for REG_CREATE_KEY_INFORMATION](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/wdm/ns-wdm-_reg_create_key_information#:~:text=If%20the%20path%20is%20absolute%2C%20this%20structure%20contains%20a%20fully%20qualified%20path%20that%20starts%20with%20the%20%22%5C%22%20character):

> If the path is absolute, this structure contains a fully qualified path that starts with the "\\" character. For an absolute path, the RootObject member specifies the \REGISTRY key.

The fix checks whether `CompleteName` starts with `\` — if so, it's already an absolute path and should be used directly without prepending the root key name. This is the documented contract for the callback structure.

## Problem

The nightly auto-regression pipeline (42 test suites run Mon-Fri against the latest main build) still runs in Azure DevOps. This needs to be migrated to GitHub Actions as part of the ongoing CI/CD migration.

## Solution

New `auto-regression.yml` workflow (\\"Run Regression\\") that:

- **Schedule**: Runs Mon-Fri at 00:01 UTC via cron, plus `workflow_dispatch` for manual triggers

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Need a way to manually run individual test suites against a specific build from GitHub Actions, replacing the AzDO `run-test-suite.yaml` pipeline.

## Solution

Adds three things:

1. **`run-test-suite.yml`** - Manual `workflow_dispatch` workflow with 13 inputs (under the 25 limit):
   - Suite selection (41 choices), build identifier (version, run ID, or \"latest\"), debug/diagnostic toggles
   - Setup job finds the build via `find-build` action, resolves the product version
   - Optional automation rebuild, then runs the suite via `reusable-run-test-suite.yml`

2. **Updated `find-build` action** - Now accepts three input formats:
   - Product version (e.g. `26.2.1.153`) - searches recent runs by downloading `_BuildVersion` artifact
   - Run ID (e.g. `24353155913`) - validates artifacts exist
   - `latest` - finds most recent run with required artifacts (no longer requires success - allows testing against builds with flaky smoke failures)
   - Always outputs both `run-id` and `product-version`

3. **`_BuildVersion` artifact in `build.yml`** - Tiny text file uploaded by the setup job containing the product version string, enabling cross-run version resolution.

Tested locally with `test-find-build.ps1` against all input paths (latest, run ID, missing artifacts, invalid input).

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

<!-- REPLACE WITH DETAILS HERE -->
After a service restart, automation tests were proceeding before the PMfW service had fully connected to the kernel driver. The service may be in the `Running` state while the driver port connection is still being established, causing tests to interact with the service before it is ready — leading to flaky failures.

When EnableProvider throws `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES (0x800705AA)`, `TraceLogListener` and `ActivityLogListener` now run `logman query -ets` and log the full session list so the cause is immediately visible in test output.

## Solution

<!-- REPLACE WITH DETAILS HERE -->
Added a `TRACE_DEBUG(L\"Connected to Driver\")` log in `FsFilterDriverProcessing.cpp` at the point where the thread pool (and therefore the driver port connection) is confirmed ready.
Added a check in `ClientConfiguration.StartDefendpointService()`, when starting the `PrivilegeManagementForWindows` service, an ETW trace capture is now started before the service launches and a Polly retry asserts the \"Connected to Driver\" log line is seen before the method returns. This ensures the PMfW service waits for the driver connection in one place.

When EnableProvider throws `ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES (0x800705AA)`, `TraceLogListener` and `ActivityLogListener` now run `logman query -ets` and log the full session list so the cause is immediately visible in test output.

`CleanupOrphanedEtwSessions()` added to `CommonSetup.ScenarioSetup()` to stop any leftover `AutomationTraceLog_*` and `AutomationActivityLog_*` sessions from previous crashed test runs before starting a new session, preventing the ETW session limit from being exhausted.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

The test suite execution pipelines need a reusable workflow that handles the core test execution logic — downloading artifacts, modifying IaC definitions, running DevOps Factory, and collecting results. This is shared between `run-test-suite.yml` (Phase 4) and `auto-regression.yml` (Phase 5).

## Solution

Add `reusable-run-test-suite.yml` — reusable workflow that executes a single test suite via DevOps Factory. Steps:

1. Downloads build artifacts from a Full Build run (cross-run download via `run-id` parameter)
2. Downloads PMC adapter/Package Manager installers from AzDO (via `download-pmc-artifacts` composite action)
3. Modifies IaC definitions based on test parameters (`ModifyIaC.ps1`)
4. Executes `BeyondTrust.DevOps.Factory.exe` with the TDEF file
5. Copies test results (.trx) and memory leak data from the network share
6. Uploads results as artifacts

Tested end-to-end with a Smoke test run — Factory provisions VMs, installs the product, runs tests, and results are collected successfully.

Key learnings during implementation:
- Factory runners need `shell: powershell` (no pwsh)
- `runner.temp` not available in job-level `env:` blocks
- Factory's `--VSTSBuildNumber` must be the product version (e.g. `26.2.1.153`), not the GitHub run ID
- AzDO Container-type artifacts need REST API download, not `az pipelines runs artifact download`

Phase 3 of the test suite execution migration.

## Problem

The xray-create skill script was doing too much — parsing, importing, fetching summaries, classifying tests, deleting duplicates, and setting test types all in a single invocation. This made it hard to debug failures, and the classification logic had bugs (duplicate detection relied on import results containing existing tests, which isn't guaranteed).

## Solution

Restructured into a clear separation of concerns:

- **Script** split into 4 modes: `-Check`, `-Import`, `-Delete`, `-SetCucumber` — each does one Xray API operation
- **Skill** handles classification logic (new/duplicate/variation) and orchestrates the calls
- Fixed duplicate detection by fetching summaries via Xray GraphQL `jira(fields: [\\"summary\\",\\"key\\"])` instead of relying on import results
- Fixed bare `@EPM-` and `@EPM-TODO` tags breaking Xray import (regex now strips the entire tag)
- Fixed inline comments on tag lines breaking Xray import
- Added `SetCucumber` mode to ensure test type is always Cucumber

body:
## Problem

PR #3619 fixed flaky challenge/auth notification tests on ARM64 by switching `FillInEditBoxWithContent` from `Keyboard.Type()` to `control.Text = content` (which routes through `IUIAutomationValuePattern.SetValue`). This was validated against challenge/auth dialogs only.

However, `SetValue` returns `E_ACCESSDENIED` for the JIT reason edit box (`IDC_REASON_EDIT`), which has an unusual configuration (`ES_AUTOHSCROLL | NOT WS_BORDER`) with a `SS_BLACKFRAME` static overlay for the visual border. This caused 25 JIT App Access Request test failures in build 345062 with `System.UnauthorizedAccessException` wrapping `E_ACCESSDENIED`.

The underlying reason both dialog types are affected is that `PGMessageHostExt.exe` runs at System integrity level, and UIPI restricts certain cross-process UI operations targeting higher-integrity windows. The challenge/auth response field (`IDC_OTP_RESPONSE_EDIT`) happens to accept `SetValue` successfully; the JIT reason field does not.

## Solution

Add a `catch (UnauthorizedAccessException)` fallback in `FillInEditBoxWithContent` that restores the original `Keyboard.Type()` approach when `SetValue` is denied. Controls that accept `SetValue` (e.g. the challenge/auth response field) are unaffected and continue using the faster path. Only controls that reject it hit the fallback.

Alternatives considered:
- **Lower PGMessageHostExt to High integrity** (Tom Beech's `test/pgmessagehost-high-integrity`, commit 82a59950f) — would fix the root cause but is a product change outside the scope of this test fix.
- **Revert PR #3619 entirely** — would reintroduce the ARM64 focus-stealing flakiness the original change fixed.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

The `create_release_branch.yml` workflow triggers an AzDO driver pipeline when cutting a release, and there's no mechanism to create the `next-release-*` git tags that the version computation system (EPM-51551) relies on. Without these tags, version computation fails on new branches.

## Solution

**Update `create_release_branch.yml`:**
- Replace AzDO driver pipeline trigger (`az pipelines run`) with GitHub `driver-build.yml` workflow dispatch (with counter-sign + update-pin enabled). The driver-build workflow's auto-pin job will create a PR to update `DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER`.
- Remove `driver-dependency-vars.yaml` update (now handled by driver-build auto-pin PR)
- Update release branch PR to reflect policy-template-only changes
- The release branch inherits the existing `next-release-*` tag from main's history — no new tag needed at branch creation

**Create `tag-next-release.yml`:**
- Triggers on push to main when `Common/ProductVersion.h` changes
- Reads the version from ProductVersion.h and creates `next-release-{major}.{minor}.1` tag
- This handles the main branch tag after the version bump PR is squash-merged (can't tag during `create_release_branch` because the PR hasn't merged yet)
- Skips if the tag already exists

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

When driver code changes are pushed to main/release, the existing `update_driver_props.yml` triggers an AzDO pipeline to build the driver and creates a PR to update the version. This needs to be migrated to use the GitHub `driver-build.yml` workflow instead. Additionally, after a driver build there's no automatic mechanism to update the `DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER` pin in `build.yml`.

## Solution

Add push trigger and auto-pin job to `driver-build.yml`:
- **Push trigger** for `PGDriver/**` on main/release branches — triggers driver build when driver code changes (absorbs `update_driver_props.yml` functionality)
- **`update-pin` input** for manual dispatch (requires counter-sign to be enabled)
- **`update-pin` job** that runs after successful counter-signing: creates a PR to update `DRIVER_BUILD_RUN_NUMBER` in `build.yml` with the new run number
  - Extracts EPM ticket number from the commit message for the PR title (falls back to `EPM-XXXXX` which fails title validation, forcing manual update)
  - Assigns the PR to the actor who triggered the run
  - Uses GitHub App token for PR creation (same pattern as existing `update_driver_props.yml`)
- Permissions scoped per-job — only the update-pin job has write access

`update_driver_props.yml` can be removed in a follow-up once this is validated.

v9.0.0

New features:

  • getOctokit factory function — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See Creating additional clients with getOctokit for details and examples.

Breaking changes:

If you previously used patterns like const { getOctokit } = require('@actions/github') to create secondary clients, use the new injected getOctokit function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.

Scripts that declare const getOctokit = ... or let getOctokit = ... will get a SyntaxError because JavaScript does not allow const/let redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected getOctokit directly, or use var getOctokit = ... if you need to redeclare it.

## Problem

## Problem

body:
## Problem

Customer reports severe system slowness on SQL servers with Agent Protection enabled (SQL jobs timing out, slow logon, `dir` takes minutes).

The Agent Protection registry callback (`RegistryCallback`) has two main performance issues:

1. It calls `GetProcessImageFileNameFromProcessHandle` (2 syscalls + 2 pool allocations) on **every registry operation** — even read-only operations and notify classes it doesn't filter.
2. When a key matches the blocked list, `HandleIsDefendpointService` resolves the process image name a second time.

Benchmark: **17x slowdown** on registry operations (44k ops/s → 2.6k ops/s) with Agent Protection enabled.

## Solution

1. **Early exit for non-write notify classes** — Only `RegNtPreCreateKey/Ex` and `RegNtPreOpenKey/Ex` need filtering. All other operations return immediately, skipping process name resolution entirely.

2. **Service process early exit** — Check `ProcessIsDefendpointService` once after resolving the process name, removing the redundant `HandleIsDefendpointService` call from `IsKeyBlockedForWrite`.

3. **HKLM prefix quick-reject** — Skip the blocked-paths iteration for non-HKLM keys, since all protected paths are under `\REGISTRY\MACHINE\`.

body:
## Problem
The test `AppControl_ChallengeANDAuth_RunAsCurrentUser` is flaky, primarily on ARM64 machines. It failed across multiple regression runs with two distinct failure modes, all rooted in FlaUI UI automation issues interacting with the EPM challenge/authentication notification dialog:

1. **Timed out waiting 1 minute for process** — On ARM64, the dialog interaction appeared to complete but `DummyApplication.AnyCPU.exe` never started, suggesting the Authorize button click or response wasn't processed correctly due to the same focus-stealing issue.
2. **NullReferenceException in FillInPassword** — `FindFirstDescendant().AsTextBox()` returns null when the password field isn't found, causing a bare NRE instead of a diagnosable assertion failure.

## Solution
Three targeted fixes addressing each failure mode:

1. **Replace `Keyboard.Type()` with `ValuePattern` in `FillInEditBoxWithContent`** (NotificationPopup.cs) — Instead of the fragile click → select-all → type sequence that depends on window focus, set the `Text` property directly on the control via UIA's ValuePattern. This writes to the control regardless of which window has focus, eliminating the ARM64 focus-stealing flakiness.
2. **Add null-check in `FillInPassword`** (NotificationPopup.cs) — Use the null-conditional operator (`?.`) on `FindFirstDescendant()` and add `Assert.IsNotNull` with a meaningful message. This replaces a bare `NullReferenceException` with a clear assertion failure that identifies which control was not found.

The C# CodeQL analysis job takes ~18 minutes and runs on every PR regardless of whether any C# files were changed. This wastes CI minutes and slows down feedback for PRs that only touch C++, workflow YAML, Python, or other non-C# files.

## Solution

Split the C# analysis out of the language matrix into its own `analyze-csharp` job with a lightweight change detection step:

1. **`analyze-csharp` — detection step** — Uses the GitHub API (`gh api`) to check if any `.cs`/`.csproj`/`.sln` files changed in the PR. Runs in seconds, no checkout needed. On API failure, defaults to running the full scan (fail-safe).
2. **`analyze`** — The fast languages (actions, JS, python, ruby) remain in the matrix, unaffected.
3. **`analyze-csharp` — analysis steps** — Always runs (satisfying the required status check and code scanning gate), but skips the expensive CodeQL init/analyze steps when no C# files changed. When skipping, uploads an empty SARIF with matching tool name and category so the code scanning merge protection is satisfied. On schedule/workflow_dispatch it always performs the full analysis.

No third-party actions added — uses the existing `gh` CLI and GitHub API.

## Problem

The test `Identity - MFA can be passed with changed user email after group refresh` ([EPM-52388](https://beyondtrust.atlassian.net/browse/EPM-52388)) was failing at the step `And the Identity cache for 'admin' is populated with 'userEmail' value 'new_email@example.com'`.

After a service restart, the mock OIDC server was configured to return a new email address. However, the test moved straight to asserting the identity cache value without first confirming that the IdP groups cache had been refreshed. Because the group refresh cycle had not yet completed, the identity cache still held the stale email (`clientuser@btrusteng.com`), causing the assertion to fail with: `Expected:<new_email@example.com>. Actual:<clientuser@btrusteng.com>`.

## Solution

Added the step `And the IdP groups cache has been refreshed` between the task tray identity verification and the identity cache assertion. This ensures the test explicitly waits for the full IdP group refresh cycle to complete before asserting on the updated cache values, eliminating the race condition that caused the failure.

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

<!-- REPLACE WITH DETAILS HERE -->
`TheProcessHasStarted` in `RunProcessBindings.cs` contained a race condition that caused intermittent failures in `AllowExecution_ShellExecuteRunAsAdmin_Commandline_BAT`.

After the task completes and returns a `Process` object, the binding was immediately calling `Process.GetProcessById(process.Id)` to create a new instance that would survive the surrounding `using` block's disposal. However, `ShellExecApplication.exe` calls the Win32 `ShellExecute(\"runas\", ...)` API, which is fire-and-forget — the process exits immediately after `ShellExecute` returns. On fast machines or with fast-resolving file types (BAT in particular), the process can exit between the task completing and `GetProcessById` executing, throwing `ArgumentException: Process with an Id of X is not running` and causing the test step to fail with an unhandled exception.

This was observed on builds 340931, 342492, and 342659, with the failure rate increasing after commit `801f9bf62` (merged 2026-03-18) changed the UAC launch path to `NativeProcessApi.LaunchNativeProcess`, altering timing characteristics.

## Solution

<!-- REPLACE WITH DETAILS HERE -->
Remove the `using` block and store the original `Process` object from the task result directly in the scenario context, rather than re-fetching it by PID. The original object is already fully populated (including `StartInfo`) and does not require re-opening — the only reason for the `using` pattern was to ensure disposal, so we now handle that explicitly with `process?.Dispose()` in the `\"does not start\"` path.

This eliminates the race entirely: the step no longer cares whether the process is still alive, only that it was successfully created — which is the correct semantic for the `\"the process has started\"` step.

## Problem

Two `UniqueAsyncQueue` unit tests intermittently fail on CI build agents (`UniqueAsyncQueue_AddJob_CheckDuplicateJobsArePermitted` and `UniqueAsyncQueue_AddJob_CheckQueueIgnoresDuplicateJob`). Both fail with `Assert failed. Expected:<258> Actual:<0>` — `WaitForSingleObject` returns `WAIT_TIMEOUT` instead of `WAIT_OBJECT_0`. The tests use 100ms timeouts for waits that should succeed, which is too tight for loaded CI agents. The negative assertion (verifying a deduped job didn't run) also relied on a timeout, which can't distinguish \"didn't run\" from \"hasn't run yet.\"

## Solution

- Increased the \"should succeed\" `WaitForSingleObject` timeouts from 100ms to 5000ms
- Replaced the timeout-based negative assertion with a deterministic `GetStarted()` flag on the mock, eliminating false positives from timing
- Fixed `Assert::AreEqual` argument order to `(expected, actual)` across all assertions for clearer failure diagnostics

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

`AntiTamper_PGDriver_ElevatedContent_RenameViaUI` fails on Windows 11 25H2 ([build 342218](https://avecto-vsts.visualstudio.com/Windows/_build/results?buildId=342218), machine B-11-25H2-01). The test opens Explorer, types `PGDriver` to select the file via type-ahead, presses F2 to enter rename mode, types the new name, and presses Enter. On 25H2, the F2 keystroke is consumed by Explorer's type-ahead search context before it can activate rename mode — so the rename is never attempted and the expected "File Access Denied" dialog never appears.

Evidence:
- The companion `DeleteViaUI` test (same `ScrollTo` → keyboard flow, minus F2) **passed** on the same machine, confirming file selection and dialog detection work fine on 25H2.
- The screenshot at failure time shows Explorer open to `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\` with no dialog visible.
- Debug logs show DACL protection was correctly applied to `PGDriver.sys` but no rename operation was intercepted by the service.
- Passed on all 15 other machines (LTSB 2016 through Server 2025).

## Solution

Add `Explorer.ActivateRenameMode()` which uses Polly to retry the F2 press until the rename Edit control actually appears in the Explorer file list, instead of blindly assuming F2 worked:

1. Press F2
2. Poll for an Edit control in the Explorer window using `FlaUI Retry.WhileNull` (1s timeout, 200ms interval)
3. If the Edit control doesn't appear, Polly retries the whole sequence (up to 3 retries, 500ms between attempts)
4. Each retry is logged for diagnostics

A `Thread.Sleep` alternative was considered but discarded — the Polly approach is self-verifying (it checks rename mode actually activated) rather than hoping a fixed delay is sufficient.

### Files changed
- **`Explorer.cs`** — new `ActivateRenameMode()` method with F2 + Polly retry + Edit control detection
- **`WindowsExplorerBindings.cs`** — replace `Keyboard.PressFunctionKey(2)` with `Explorer.ActivateRenameMode()`

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners persist their `.git/` directory between jobs. Remote-tracking refs, tags, and PR merge refs accumulate as loose files and packed refs. On subsequent runs, `actions/checkout` fails with `reference already exists` when git tries to write refs that already exist in a different form — causing intermittent CI failures that require manual re-runs.

## Solution

Adds a runner-level pre-job hook deployed via the existing ansible role. The hook runs before every job and clears stale remote-tracking refs and tags by:

1. Removing loose ref files under `.git/refs/remotes/` and `.git/refs/tags/`
2. Filtering those entries from `.git/packed-refs`

This fixes the issue globally — no workflow changes required, and new workflows automatically get the fix. The script scans all `.git` directories under the runner work directory, runs in ~95ms, and always exits 0 (best-effort cleanup that never blocks a job).

The hook is configured via `ACTIONS_RUNNER_HOOK_JOB_STARTED` in the runner's `.env` file, with the script deployed to `C:\actions-runner-hooks\` (outside the runner directory, per [GitHub's requirements](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/hosting-your-own-runners/managing-self-hosted-runners/running-scripts-before-or-after-a-job)).

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7...v8.0.0

v7.0.0

v7 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v7 now runs on Node.js 24 (runs.using: node24) and requires a minimum Actions Runner version of 2.327.1. If you are using self-hosted runners, ensure they are updated before upgrading.

Node.js 24

This release updates the runtime to Node.js 24. v6 had preliminary support for Node 24, however this action was by default still running on Node.js 20. Now this action by default will run on Node.js 24.

What's Changed

  • Update GHES guidance to include reference to Node 20 version by @​patrikpolyak in actions/download-artifact#440
  • Download Artifact Node24 support by @​salmanmkc in actions/download-artifact#415
  • fix: update @​actions/artifact to fix Node.js 24 punycode deprecation by @​salmanmkc in actions/download-artifact#451

<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD041 -->
## Problem

A support case was raised concerning an issue with the uninstallation processing that the EPM-W service performs.

When software is uninstalled from a system, EPM intercepts this uninstallation to provide elevation to the uninstaller application. For exe uninstallers, the service needs to read the `UninstallString` registry key value for the specified registered software and decipher the program that will be launched to uninstall the program.

The code to extract the program path from this `UninstallString` command line string is `icl::SplitCommandLineIntoFileAndParams`. 

## Solution

In this case, this function was unable to determine the file path correctly, and thus attempts to launch the uninstaller with an invalid path.

This PR fixes this issue by rewriting the file path extraction code to use a regular expression to extract the path found in the command line.

Add a standardized, evidence-based triage framework for EPM Jira issues that mention Windows Insider Preview Builds. Currently, triage decisions lack consistency and rigorous impact assessment of Windows changes on EPM-Windows features.

## Solution

- **Evidence-based triage flow**: fetches full Insider blog content, maps Windows changes to EPM feature areas, infers concrete EPM-W test focus

- **Jira comment format**: posts concise, scannable triage summaries with recommendation, confidence, rationale, impact areas, and test focus
- **Codebase integration**: cross-references epm-windows source modules, test suites, and Xray repository knowledge to ground recommendations

## Problem

`TaskScheduler_OnlyReadyTasksAreRan` was intermittently hanging in CI builds. The hang is a deadlock caused by a race condition in `MockConditionVariable::wait_until`.

`TaskRunner` acquires `m_taskListLock` and then calls `wait_until`. The real `std::condition_variable_any::wait_until` atomically releases the lock during the wait and reacquires it before calling the predicate. The mock did neither — it held the lock for the entire spin duration.

When the OS scheduled the `TaskRunner` thread before the main test thread could finish calling `Register()`, the TaskRunner would enter `wait_until` while holding `m_taskListLock`. Each `Register()` call then blocked trying to acquire that lock, and since `waitForTaskRun()` had not been called yet, `locked` was never set to `false` to unblock the spin — resulting in a deadlock/hang.

## Solution

Add `lock.unlock()` before the spin loop and `lock.lock()` after it in `MockConditionVariable::wait_until`. This matches the semantics of `std::condition_variable_any::wait_until`, which releases the associated mutex during the wait and reacquires it before returning.

No changes to production code are needed — the race is entirely in the test mock.

## Problem

When certain older applications are executed, windows may apply a number of shims via an Application Compatibility DLL (AcSpecfc.dll), which can hook a number of win32 API functions. In the case of some old installers being executed as SYSTEM, this can cause PGHook to fail when loading via the APC method, as it is loaded after AcSpecfc, which then attempts to load a library while PGHook is being injected (Actual hang occurs during CRT setup code in PGHook, just before DLLMmain would be called). 
This issue does not occur with IDT, as that ensures PGHook is loaded before the shim.

## Solution

Repurpose the existing DriverInjectionFallback registry key, which will now allow the specified executables to run with the non-default injection method:

If the default injection method is set as APC, and some application is specified in the key, the driver will use the IDT method instead of APC to inject into it.
If IDT is the default, then the entries in the registry + a built-in list of exclusions is checked. If the application matches, then it will fallback to APC.
